items.title: Enfants en ligne: l’ONU appelle à agir contre les risques de l’IA et de la désinformation
items.description: Plus de huit jeunes sur dix âgés de 15 à 24 ans dans le monde sont désormais connectés à Internet. Dans les pays à faible revenu, leur taux de connexion est même près de deux fois supérieur à celui du reste de la population. Cette génération hyperconnectée est pourtant particulièrement exposée aux risques qui menacent l’intégrité de l’information, notamment la désinformation, le harcèlement en ligne, les biais algorithmiques et l’utilisation malveillante de l’intelligence artificielle (IA), alerte l’ONU lundi. Dans une nouvelle note publiée à l’approche de la Journée internationale de la jeunesse, l’Organisation exhorte les États membres, les entreprises technologiques, les annonceurs, les médias et les chercheurs à faire de la protection et de la participation des enfants et des jeunes une priorité. Le mois dernier, le Secrétaire général de l’ONU, António Guterres , avait appelé à renforcer la sécurité des enfants face à l’IA, comparant les technologies émergentes à des médicaments non testés et plaidant pour une réglementation plus stricte. «Aucun enfant ne devrait servir de cobaye pour une IA non réglementée… Lorsqu'un enfant subit un préjudice, la réponse ne doit jamais être « c'est la faute de l'algorithme »», avait déclaré M. Guterres en juillet, lors du premier Dialogue mondial sur la gouvernance de l’IA. Des préjudices qui ne sont pas accidentels La note souligne que les préjudices auxquels les jeunes sont confrontés en ligne ne sont pas le fruit du hasard. Ils découlent notamment de modèles économiques fondés sur la monétisation de l’attention et des données personnelles, ainsi que de choix de conception destinés à maximiser l’engagement et les dépenses. Algorithmes conçus pour maintenir les jeunes utilisateurs en ligne, «schémas obscurs» (dark patterns), coffres à butin (loot boxes) et autres mécanismes favorisant une utilisation compulsive sont autant de pratiques qui peuvent les exposer à des risques particuliers. Les enfants sont d’autant plus vulnérables que leurs habitudes, leur identité et leurs relations sont encore en pleine formation. L’IA, poursuit le document, progresse plus rapidement que les efforts visant à encadrer son adoption. Elle amplifie ainsi des risques allant de la diffusion de contenus générés par IA à l’exploitation facilitée par ces technologies. La note alerte également sur des pratiques publicitaires de plus en plus difficiles à identifier, qui cherchent à influencer les enfants et à accroître leurs dépenses en ligne. «Dans leur ensemble, ces pratiques banalisent une surveillance commerciale omniprésente et une conception manipulative à une période où les enfants et les jeunes sont les plus influençables», indique le document. Des acteurs, pas seulement des victimes Les enfants et les jeunes ne sont toutefois pas seulement des victimes potentielles, souligne l’ONU. Ils sont aussi créateurs, journalistes, défenseurs de causes et organisateurs de mouvements qui contribuent à façonner le débat public et la vie civique. Mais les mêmes espaces numériques qui permettent à ces mouvements de se développer exposent leurs acteurs — souvent de jeunes femmes, des membres de minorités ou des militants — au harcèlement et à la surveillance en ligne. Pour l’ONU, les jeunes doivent donc être davantage associés à la recherche et à l’élaboration des politiques destinées à répondre aux menaces pesant sur l’intégrité de l’information. «Les enfants et les jeunes figurent parmi les personnes les plus touchées par la crise actuelle de l’information, mais aussi parmi celles les plus à même de contribuer à la résoudre», a déclaré Charlotte Scaddan, conseillère principale de l’ONU pour l’intégrité de l’information. «Les protéger et les inclure ne sont pas des objectifs contradictoires. Nous devons faire les deux.» Une fenêtre d’action qui se referme La sécurité des enfants en ligne s’est imposée au cœur des débats politiques, notamment autour des fonctionnalités favorisant l’addiction, de la publicité comportementale, de la modération des contenus et de la protection de la vie privée. Mais face à l’essor rapide de l’IA, l’ONU estime que la fenêtre d’opportunité pour inscrire les droits de l’enfant dans les cadres de gouvernance de cette technologie se réduit rapidement. La note appelle ainsi les États à renforcer les cadres législatifs, les entreprises technologiques à intégrer la sécurité des enfants dès la conception de leurs produits, les annonceurs à respecter leurs droits, les médias à mieux s’adresser aux jeunes publics et les chercheurs à combler les lacunes existantes, notamment dans les pays du Sud. L’ONU poursuit parallèlement ses efforts pour contribuer à une meilleure gouvernance de l’IA, notamment à travers le Dialogue mondial sur la gouvernance de l’IA et le Groupe scientifique international indépendant sur l’IA , chargé d’évaluer les opportunités et les risques liés à cette technologie. « Alors que les technologies numériques et les environnements informationnels continuent d’évoluer, le moment est venu de passer, de toute urgence, des principes à l’action concrète », conclut le document. Source: ONU Info L’article Enfants en ligne: l’ONU appelle à agir contre les risques de l’IA et de la désinformation est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

Pétanque : Les Étalons médaillés à Abidjan célébrés par la Fédération
items.description: La Fédération burkinabè de pétanque (FBP) a organisé, le 8 août 2026 à Yagma, une cérémonie de célébration en l'honneur des Étalons boulistes ayant pris part à la compétition de la Zone 2 Afrique de l'Ouest de la Confédération africaine de sport pétanque, à Abidjan. La délégation burkinabè, conduite par l'entraîneur national Djibril Ouédraogo, est rentrée au pays avec deux médailles, dont une en or et une en bronze, ainsi que deux trophées. La Fédération a également associé à cette célébration les boulistes ayant participé à l'immersion patriotique. La Fédération burkinabè de pétanque (FBP), avec à sa tête son président, Isidore Kientéga, et l'ensemble de son staff, a organisé, le 8 août 2026 à Yagma, une cérémonie de célébration des Étalons boulistes ayant pris part à la compétition de la Zone 2 Afrique de l'Ouest de la Confédération africaine de sport pétanque, à Abidjan. Les Étalons Patrice Tiemtoré, Aziz Ouédraogo, Nestor Zoromé et Madi Tapsoba, conduits par l'entraîneur national Djibril Ouédraogo, ont regagné le pays avec deux médailles, dont une en or et une en bronze, ainsi que deux trophées. À cette occasion, la Fédération a associé à la célébration les boulistes qui sont allés accomplir l'immersion patriotique. Le quatuor d'Étalons boulistes, de gauche à droite : Djibril Ouédraogo, l'entraîneur national, Patrice Tiemtoré, Madi Tapsoba, Aziz Ouédraogo et Nestor Zoromé. Pour cette cérémonie, la grande famille bouliste a été conviée. On notait notamment la présence du président de la Ligue du Centre de pétanque, Adolphe Bamogo, du président de la Zone 2 Afrique de l'Ouest, Arsène Macaire Kaboré, des présidents de clubs et de districts, ainsi que des autorités coutumières et administratives. Plusieurs interventions ont ponctué le cérémonial. Le Naaba Kougri de Cella, par ailleurs secrétaire chargé des relations de la FBP, a souhaité la bienvenue à tous ceux qui ont effectué le déplacement pour soutenir la Fédération dans cette initiative qu'il a qualifiée de louable. Selon lui, celle-ci vise à magnifier les athlètes et à dire bravo aux boulistes ainsi qu'aux membres de la FBP ayant accepté d'aller à l'immersion patriotique. À ce sujet, le représentant des immergés patriotes, Adama Kagoné, du club Arc-en-ciel, a fait savoir que l'immersion s'est déroulée en deux phases : théorique et pratique. Elle a porté sur l'éveil et l'affermissement du sentiment patriotique, ainsi que sur les comportements de défense à adopter dans le contexte sécuritaire que vit le pays. Les officiels à la cérémonie de célébration. La compétition de pétanque d'Abidjan, elle, a concerné quatre spécialités : la doublette, la triplette, le tir de précision et le tête-à-tête masculin. Le Burkina Faso, par l'entremise d'Aziz Ouédraogo, s'est adjugé la médaille d'or en tir de précision et la médaille de bronze avec Madi Tapsoba en tête-à-tête masculin. En rappel, le tournoi, qui s'est déroulé du 21 au 24 mai 2026, a regroupé le Bénin, le Burkina Faso, le pays hôte, la Côte d'Ivoire, le Niger, la Guinée et le Mali, avec environ une trentaine de joueurs. La cérémonie de célébration avait connu deux reports pour des cas de force majeure. À l'occasion de cette rencontre, les Étalons ont solennellement présenté leurs trophées et leurs médailles à la FBP ainsi qu'à l'assistance. Le contingent des membres de la FBP et des boulistes à l'immersion patriotique. « Tout l'honneur revient à la Fédération burkinabè de pétanque, parce que nous sommes les premiers gagnants, et les plus grands gagnants. Étalons boulistes, soyez fiers de ce que vous avez accompli comme mission à Abidjan, chers immergés patriotes, soyez fiers d'avoir répondu à l'appel de la patrie pour accomplir un acte hautement citoyen », a salué le président de la FBP, Isidore Kientéga, à l'endroit des Étalons boulistes et des immergés patriotes. Il a poursuivi en exhortant les boulistes à toujours viser l'excellence dans tout ce qu'ils font. Selon lui, ils ne le font pour personne, mais pour porter haut les couleurs de la nation. En guise de récompense, la FBP a promis de faire un geste pour eux. Le cérémonial a pris fin autour d'un repas convivial. Barthélemy Kaboré (Collaborateur)

items.title: Anti-Witchcraft Accusations Bill advances as Gender Ministry engages Amnesty International Ghana
items.description: The Anti-Witchcraft Accusations Bill is progressing through the required processes, with proposed amendments to the Criminal Offences Act currently before the Attorney General’s Department. The update was disclosed by the Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection, Dr Agnes Naa Momo Lartey, during a meeting with a delegation from Amnesty International Ghana led by its Director, Hannah Osei. The meeting focused on the progress of the Bill and measures to strengthen the protection of persons affected by accusations of witchcraft. Ms Osei commended the Ministry for its efforts to advance gender equality and social protection and reaffirmed Amnesty International Ghana’s commitment to supporting advocacy for the passage of the Bill. She urged the Ministry to continue working with the Attorney General’s Department and other stakeholders to facilitate the Bill’s progress. According to her, reintroducing the legislation as a government-sponsored Bill could help address some of the challenges that prevented its earlier passage. Dr Lartey welcomed Amnesty International Ghana’s continued partnership and reiterated the Ministry’s commitment to protecting vulnerable persons through stronger legal and policy measures. The Minister said the Bill is going through the necessary processes, with proposed amendments to the Criminal Offences Act currently under consideration by the Attorney General’s Department. The two sides also discussed opportunities for continued collaboration to protect the rights, dignity and well-being of persons affected by witchcraft accusations. The engagement forms part of ongoing efforts to strengthen Ghana’s legal and policy framework for protecting vulnerable persons and addressing harmful practices associated with accusations of witchcraft.

items.title: Tivaouane : le Service d’hygiène lance ses activités pour l’édition 2026 du Gamou
items.description: Le Service d’hygiène a lancé, ce mardi 11 août 2026, son dispositif de couverture sanitaire, en prélude au Gamou 2026. La cérémonie a été présidée par l’adjoint au gouverneur de Thiès, Babacar Sadikh Niang, en présence de l’adjoint au préfet de Tivaouane et des autorités locales. Pour cette édition, 204 agents sont mobilisés, dont 100 par la mairie, avec un important dispositif matériel comprenant notamment des drones. « Ce dispositif, dirigé par le directeur régional de la Santé de Thiès, vise à assurer la sécurité sanitaire des populations lors de ce grand rassemblement », a expliqué le capitaine Armand Seck, commandant de la Brigade régionale d’hygiène de Thiès. Les agents sont répartis en deux groupes. Une place importante a été accordée aux femmes afin d’assurer une « sensibilisation continue » au niveau des domiciles. Les délégués de quartier et les acteurs communautaires sont également associés au dispositif. La stratégie repose sur trois axes, a annoncé le capitaine Seck. Il s’agit d’abord de déployer une communication à travers les radios, les télévisions locales et des caravanes de sensibilisation qui sillonneront la commune. La police de l’hygiène, avec un renforcement des contrôles sur la sécurité sanitaire des aliments, constitue le deuxième axe de la stratégie. Le commandant de la Brigade régionale d’hygiène a rappelé l’interception, la semaine dernière, d’un camion transportant des boissons impropres à la consommation. « Tout commerçant qui introduira des produits impropres sera interpellé », a-t-il averti. La salubrité publique constitue le troisième axe. Il s’agit notamment d’éliminer les gîtes larvaires et les dépôts d’ordures afin de prévenir les maladies liées aux inondations et à l’encombrement. Le démarrage précoce de la lutte antivectorielle fait également partie du dispositif prévu cette année. Une évaluation des risques sera effectuée à l’aide de drones afin de cibler les zones les plus sensibles. « Les drones vont nous appuyer au fur et à mesure de l’avancée du dispositif », a précisé le capitaine Armand Seck. Le capitaine a salué l’intégration des délégués de quartier dans cette nouvelle démarche, qui vise à renforcer la sensibilisation de proximité en amont du Gamou. L’adjoint au gouverneur de Thiès a, pour sa part, salué l’engagement communautaire et la synergie d’action entre les différents services. Il a invité les populations à dénoncer les comportements suspects. Ibrahima NDIAYE Correspondant

items.title: Police nab 27 year old man for allegedly defiling teenage domestic worker in Ondo
items.description: By Dayo Johnson Akure Police detectives in Ondo State have arrested a 27-year-old man, Solomon Onaola, for the alleged defilement of a 15-year-old domestic help. Vanguard gathered in Akure, the state capital, that the incident occurred in Omifon, Odigbo council area of the state. It was learnt that the guardian of the victim reported at the police station that the 15-year-old girl, who was working as a domestic help in her household, had on several occasions left home without permission. The case was initially reported at Odigbo Divisional Police Station and was subsequently transferred to the Gender-Based Offences Unit of the Command for discreet investigation, owing to the sensitive nature of the allegation. A police source said that when the girl was questioned about where she usually went whenever she left home, she allegedly disclosed that the suspect, Solomon Onaola, had been taking her to his late mother’s residence in Omifon, where he allegedly engaged in unlawful sexual intercourse with her. Contacted, the state Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Jimoh Abayomi, said: “Following the report, police operatives commenced investigation and subsequently arrested the suspect.” Abayomi added that “the victim has also been placed under appropriate care and necessary steps are being taken in accordance with established procedures for cases involving alleged sexual offences against minors.” According to him, “the Commissioner of Police, Ondo State Command, CP Felix Ohagwu, has directed the Gender-Based Offences Unit to conduct a thorough and professional investigation into the matter, with a view to establishing the facts and ensuring that justice is served.” He reiterated the command’s commitment to “protecting children and other vulnerable members of society from sexual exploitation, abuse and other forms of violence.” “Parents, guardians and members of the public are equally urged to remain vigilant, pay close attention to the welfare of children under their care and promptly report any suspected case of abuse to the police,” he said. Abayomi stated that “the suspect remains in police custody while investigation is ongoing and will be charged to court upon conclusion of investigations.” *** Suspected armed robber arrested in Owo with firearm Meanwhile, a 32-year-old suspected armed robber, Ogunmola Oluwasola, has been arrested with a firearm and ammunition in Owo. The suspect was arrested by operatives of the Command’s Anti-Kidnapping Squad during a stop-and-search operation along the Owo–Ute road. During the search, the operatives recovered one cut-to-size pistol and four rounds of live ammunition from his possession. The suspect was immediately taken into custody, while the recovered firearm and ammunition have been secured as exhibits. DSP Abayomi said the suspect’s statement had been obtained as detectives intensified efforts to establish the source of the weapon, his intended use of the firearm, and whether he is connected to any robbery, kidnapping or other criminal activities within Owo and its environs. He reiterated that the Command would continue to sustain intelligence-led patrols, stop-and-search operations and other proactive security measures across the state, particularly along major highways and identified crime-prone locations. He warned criminals and individuals who unlawfully possess or traffic in firearms that the police and other security agencies would continue to pursue them relentlessly. “The suspect remains in police custody as investigation continues, with a view to determining his possible links to other criminal activities and bringing all persons found culpable to justice,” he said. He assured members of the public that “the Command remains committed to protecting lives and property and will continue to deploy intelligence, visibility patrols and community-based policing strategies towards maintaining peace and security across the state.” The post Police nab 27 year old man for allegedly defiling teenage domestic worker in Ondo appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Apostolic Nuncio commends Mahama’s support, pledges prayers for Ghana
items.description: The Apostolic Nuncio to Ghana, Archbishop Julien Kaboré, has commended President John Dramani Mahama and his government for their commitment to the dignity of the human person, the welfare of citizens and the promotion of peace and stability. Archbishop Kaboré expressed particular appreciation for the support extended by President Mahama and the government to faith-based institutions and initiatives aimed at promoting national cohesion, stressing that the welfare and dignity of human beings must remain at the heart of governance and public service. He was speaking at the installation of Most Rev John Alphonse Asiedu, SVD of the newly established Catholic Diocese of Donkorkrom. “We pray for the government machinery and for President Mahama, so that together we can work for peace to prevail in our region,” Archbishop Kaboré said. He expressed gratitude to President Mahama for the support and goodwill extended to the Church and other faith communities, describing such collaboration as important in confronting challenges that affect society and strengthening peaceful coexistence. The Nuncio also praised the work of the Presidential Envoy for Interfaith and Ecumenical Relations, Mr Elvis Afriyie-Ankrah, for his efforts to deepen dialogue and cooperation among Ghana’s religious communities and traditional authorities. He thanked Mr Afriyie-Ankrah for his role in bringing faith leaders together and for creating platforms through which religious leaders could engage the government on issues affecting the nation and the wider region. His remarks come against the backdrop of growing calls for stronger collaboration among governments, religious institutions and traditional authorities in addressing conflicts and other threats to peace in West Africa. The Archbishop has previously highlighted the importance of peace, human dignity and solidarity in responding to challenges confronting communities in the region. During a visit to Ghana’s Upper East Region, he also expressed appreciation to government and people for their hospitality and assistance to people fleeing instability in Burkina Faso. His latest message therefore reinforces the growing recognition of Ghana as a country where religious and traditional leaders can work alongside the state to strengthen peace, social cohesion and national development. Archbishop Kaboré, a Burkinabè prelate and experienced Vatican diplomat, was appointed Apostolic Nuncio to Ghana by the Holy See in June 2024 and elevated to the dignity of Archbishop. Before his appointment to Ghana, he served in various diplomatic missions of the Holy See, including Kenya, Papua New Guinea, Costa Rica, South Korea, Croatia, Trinidad and Tobago, the Philippines and Ireland. Concluding his remarks, the Nuncio expressed his gratitude to President John Dramani Mahama, the entire government machinery, Elvis Afriyie-Ankrah and the traditional leaders present, reaffirming the Church’s commitment to working with all stakeholders for the promotion of peace, unity and the welfare of humanity.

items.title: Selective justice claims false, lawyers only trying to delay cases — Deputy AG
items.description: Deputy Attorney-General and Minister for Justice, Justice Srem-Sai, has rejected allegations of selective justice in the Chief Justice’s decision to direct selected courts to sit during the legal vacation. He described the allegation as “completely false”, insisting that several judges across the country have been designated as vacation judges and are currently conducting cases. “It is completely false. There are so many judges that are doing vacation court and there are other cases that we are conducting oral cases which are not in the vacation because their judges in those courts have not been appointed as vacation court and they’ve vacated,” he said. “So it is a false allegation they are making.” His comments come amid a growing dispute between the judiciary and the Ghana Bar Association (GBA) over the conduct of court proceedings during the legal vacation, which runs from August 1 to September 30. Justice Srem-Sai maintained that lawyers who have legitimate difficulties appearing during the vacation are not without recourse. He said counsel who cannot attend a particular sitting should appear before the court, explain the circumstances and formally seek an adjournment. “If a lawyer has a challenge which will prevent him from conducting a case on any day, what you do is to come to court and tell the court your reason, and the court will understand and grant you adjournment,” he explained. He rejected the suggestion that lawyers can simply decline to practise because the courts are on vacation. “But to sit at home and in your office and declare that because of legal vacation you have decided that you won’t practice law — of course you will decide that you won’t practice law — but clearly that does not stop the court proceedings from going,” he added. The Deputy Attorney-General further dismissed the controversy surrounding the Chief Justice’s directive, accusing lawyers of using repeated objections and requests for adjournments to delay proceedings. “As far as we are concerned, there is no controversy on this matter. It is just an attempt to, as usual, delay cases,” he said. Justice Srem-Sai pointed to what he described as a recurring pattern in some of the cases affected by the directive. “Look, what we are doing — these cases — you will notice that it’s always a fight taking dates. Every day there’s one excuse or the other whenever we want to take adjournment. This is part of the same trick,” he said. His comments come against the backdrop of the GBA’s position that Vacation Courts have traditionally been limited largely to urgent and interlocutory matters, rather than full trials. The association has also argued that the availability and willingness of counsel have historically been an important consideration in determining whether substantive proceedings should continue during the legal vacation. Justice Srem-Sai has rejected that interpretation, insisting that the authority to determine when courts sit rests with the judiciary and not the legal profession. The disagreement has intensified following the Chief Justice’s warrant directing selected courts and judges to continue hearing certain cases during the current legal vacation. The GBA has raised concerns about the practice, while the Attorney-General’s Office maintains that the designated judges have the authority to conduct proceedings during the period. The issue has particular significance for several high-profile criminal cases whose proceedings have been scheduled during the vacation. Justice Srem-Sai said the Chief Justice’s warrant remains in force and the designated courts are expected to continue with their work. He also warned that lawyers who deliberately fail to appear could leave their clients without legal representation during proceedings. In some of the affected cases, judges have directed that where counsel fails to appear, clients may be required to conduct aspects of their cases themselves, including cross-examination. The dispute therefore remains centred on the balance between the legal profession’s established practice during judicial vacations and the judiciary’s authority to ensure that cases proceed without unnecessary delays.

Two Obuasi SecTech teachers arrested over alleged assault on headmaster
items.description: Two teachers of Obuasi Senior High Technical School have been arrested by police over their alleged involvement in an attack on the school’s headmaster, Abdulai Zakaria. Police say preliminary investigations indicate that the two teachers, whose identities have not yet been disclosed, allegedly instigated students to attack the headmaster. The incident occurred on August 5, 2026, following tensions on campus. Some students accused the headmaster of involvement in ritual activities and also alleged inappropriate relationships with female students. Obuasi District Police Commander, Superintendent Mahama Iddrisu, told JoyNews that three teachers were initially picked up for questioning after the headmaster gave a formal statement to police. According to him, investigations later focused on two of the teachers, who are expected to be put before court. “The headmaster was attacked. He was hospitalised. After he was released, he gave a statement to the police and, in the statement he gave, he mentioned certain names. He says there were students who attacked him and there were teachers who instigated them to attack him,” he said. Read Also: Obuasi SecTech headteacher hospitalised after students assaulted him for allegedly burying a fetus “Initially, there were three people that we picked yesterday, and then we investigated. We took their statements and through their statements and the headmaster’s statement, we see that they have a lot of questions to answer. “So, as I’m speaking now, we are putting them before court this morning so that we seek for remand. Maybe the court will remand them to police custody for us to continue with our investigations. The two suspects are teachers of the SecTech school,” he added. Police probe foetus found on campus Superintendent Iddrisu also disclosed that police are awaiting an autopsy and possible DNA examination on a male foetus that was exhumed from a location on the school campus. The foetus, which was recovered on August 5, is currently being kept at the Obuasi Government Hospital morgue. “It is true that a baby boy was buried on the campus of the school, very far from the dormitory. Our information was that the students saw it and then went and exhumed it, and then they are putting false allegations that it is the headmaster or they are alleging that it is the headmaster who buried it, without any evidence or eyewitness or any video saying that they have seen him,” he said. He added that the suspicion surrounding the burial contributed to the attack on the headmaster. “The body of the baby boy has been taken by the police to the Obuasi Government Hospital for preservation and maybe we will do a post-mortem examination and, if possible, a DNA test to know exactly who brought it, if it is the headmaster or any other person,” Superintendent Iddrisu said. Meanwhile, the headmaster, who sustained machete injuries during the attack, has since been discharged from hospital.

items.title: GBA got it completely wrong on legal vacation — Deputy A-G
items.description: Deputy Attorney-General (A-G) and Minister for Justice, Dr Justice Srem-Sai, has dismissed the Ghana Bar Association’s (GBA) position on legal vacation as having no basis in law, describing it as a “self-imposed understanding” that cannot be allowed to undermine the administration of justice. According to him, there is no genuine controversy over whether courts can sit and conduct proceedings during the legal vacation, insisting that vacation courts have always been constituted to deal with cases during the period. Dr Srem-Sai said the assertion that lawyers could determine whether proceedings should take place during legal vacations was unsupported by law, practice or reason. “No genuine or real controversy here. The matter is simple. It’s been the case that vacation courts are always sitting whenever there is a legal vacation,” he said. He stressed that the authority to determine when courts sit rests with the judiciary and not lawyers appearing before them. “No one can dispute that simple fact. The claim that it is the lawyers who decide whether they want to have proceedings on vacation is not founded on any facts; it’s not founded on any law, it’s not founded on reason, and it is not founded on any rule of practice. Nowhere in the world do you see lawyers deciding when a court should sit,” he added. ‘GBA got it completely wrong’ The Deputy Attorney-General’s comments come amid a disagreement between the government and the GBA over the conduct of court proceedings during the current legal vacation. Dr Srem-Sai said the Chief Justice had issued warrants authorising a number of judges to sit during the vacation to deal with cases assigned to them. “What matters is that the head of the judiciary has given warrants for a number of judges, I think 10 or more judges, to sit across the country to take care of cases,” he said. He explained that a judge assigned to a vacation court had the authority to administer his or her court during that period, arguing that accepting the GBA’s interpretation would create further delays when the legal vacation ended. “Now this is a thing; a vacation judge has his own courts to administer. Now when the vacation is over, he is also entitled to go on vacation; that is, after October,” he said. Dr Srem-Sai argued that if vacation judges were prevented from hearing cases during the legal vacation, cases before them could face prolonged delays because those same judges could subsequently proceed on leave when the courts formally resumed. “If you make the argument, as the GBA president is making, that a vacation judge is not required or cannot hear cases or conduct trial, then when the vacation is over and he goes on vacation, no other judge can have trial for them,” he said. He said such an interpretation could effectively mean that some cases would not be heard until January next year, given the sequence of the legal vacation and subsequent court recesses. “So basically what the GBA is saying is that for cases that are pending in the courts that have vacation judges, those cases can only conduct trials in January next year,” he said. Order 79 cited Dr Srem-Sai further rejected the suggestion that there was a convention preventing lawyers from conducting proceedings during legal vacations. “And again, it is not supported by reason that would be positive or advance the cause of justice. So for us, it is a self-imposed understanding of the law, which we do not think should be allowed to prevail,” he said. He pointed specifically to Order 79 of the High Court (Civil Procedure) Rules, 2004 (C.I. 47), which deals with sittings, office hours and vacations. Order 79 Rule 1 provides that, subject to the Courts Act, the Chief Justice may appoint any day, including vacation periods, for the hearing of causes or matters as circumstances require. Dr Srem-Sai therefore said the GBA’s claim that there was a convention preventing such proceedings was incorrect. “And they claim that there is a convention is completely even false. There is no such convention. And even if there is a convention, order 79 of CI 47 is the order that provides expressly for legal vacation,” he said. Lawyers’ absence The Deputy Attorney-General also addressed the possible consequences for lawyers who decline to appear before a court during the vacation. He said a vacation judge who had been duly authorised to hear a case could proceed with the matter, and lawyers could not unilaterally prevent the court from sitting. He said clients whose lawyers decided not to practise during the vacation should be advised of the implications, particularly where their cases involved active proceedings. “If you don’t come, he will treat it as if you are not interested in legal representation,” Dr Srem-Sai said. He added that where an accused person failed to produce legal representation at the next adjourned date, the court could require the person to proceed without counsel, subject to the applicable legal safeguards. “If on the next adjournment date, he does not produce, I think the judge has given them one week. If they do not produce a lawyer, then they will have to conduct the cross-examination by themselves,” he said. The dispute comes against the background of wider concerns over delays in the prosecution of corruption and other high-profile criminal cases. Dr Srem-Sai has previously said that the Attorney-General’s Office has identified about 30 cases under the Operation Recover All Loot (ORAL) initiative considered prosecutable, with between five and 10 already at advanced stages before the courts. The Deputy Attorney-General has also previously indicated that prosecutors intended to use the legal vacation period to file additional ORAL cases. His latest comments underline the government’s position that legal vacation should not become an impediment to the timely administration of justice where judges have been duly authorised to sit.

items.title: GTA’s data collection model is defective – Francis Doku
items.description: The Chief Operations Officer of Maestro Africa Group, Francis Doku, has said the Ghana Tourism Authority’s data collection model fails to accurately capture tourism’s contribution to Ghana’s economy. He has therefore urged the Ghana Tourism Authority (GTA) to upgrade its model for data collection. Francis told Joy FM ’s arts and culture journalist Kwame Dadzie on 8 August 2026, during the ninth Showbiz Roundtable , that because the Authority has not properly set up its Tourism Satellite Account, it is unable to capture the real value of tourism receipts. “What we need to work on going forward is to improve how we collect the data. There is something called Tourism Satellite Account, which is what separates your tourism revenue from any other thing that will come into the market, like your own people outside who remit money into country, other things that you get from revenues and all that. If you set up your account properly, you are able to properly know. I think that because we have not properly set up our account, we are picking figures that do not properly represent the true picture,” he said. He cited Ghana Tourism Authority’s 2025 annual report which says about 1.3 million people arrived in Ghana in the year and each of them spent an average of GH¢3,320. That, he argued, produces an unrealistic figure. “It’s very defective,” he noted. Francis Doku also indicated that how the tourism revenue is calculated is a bit difficult because “if we got 3.84 billion dollars coming into the economy in 2025, a lot of the problems that we are financially will be solved.” He advised that if the Tourism Satellite Account is properly set up, every amount of money that comes into the country through tourism will be reflected in the account. The ninth Showbiz Roundtable was themed “Assessing 20 Months of Government’s Impact on Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts.” The programme examined the government’s commitments to the sector, assessed the level of implementation, measured the impact of policies and explored the road ahead for Ghana’s creative economy. The discussion featured industry figures including Chief Operations Officer of Maestro Africa Group, Francis Doku; Lead Consultant at Jesse Agyepong and Associates, Jesse Agyepong; pop culture journalist Olele Salvador; and Joy FM broadcaster Ken Addy. Also in attendance were comedians Lekzy DeComic, Kojo Pjay, Percy Obrempong, James Brown and Jacinta. Others were broadcasters Austine Woode and Kojo Preko Dankwah, while tourism professional Emmanuel Frimpong was also present. The discussion was moderated by broadcaster and arts and culture journalist Kwame Dadzie. It was produced by Philip Nai, with support from Anita Teye and Idah Lamaire.

items.title: Ghana’s merchandise trade increases to US$52.5bn in 2025 from US$6bn in 2004
items.description: Ghana’s merchandise trade increased from US$6 billion in 2004 to US$52.5 billion in 2025, according to the latest report by the Ghana Statistical Service (GSS). ‎The report, titled “Ghana’s Merchandise Trade Statistics, 2004–2025: Two Decades in Review,” provides a 21-year assessment of the country’s merchandise trade performance. ‎It shows that Ghana has gradually shifted from years of trade deficits to recording surpluses in recent years. ‎The country recorded trade surpluses in 2011, 2014, 2018, 2019, 2023, 2024 and 2025. ‎The surplus increased from GH¢5.3 billion in 2023 to GH¢44.7 billion in 2024, before rising significantly to GH¢148.3 billion in 2025. ‎ Gold dominates exports ‎Gold has strengthened its position as Ghana’s leading export commodity. ‎Its share of Ghana’s exports increased from 38.5 percent in 2004 to 63.1 percent in 2025. ‎In contrast, cocoa beans and cocoa products accounted for 29.3 percent of exports in 2004 but declined to 14 percent in 2025. ‎Mineral fuels and oils accounted for 8.8 percent of exports in 2025. ‎Ghana’s Merchandise Trade Statistics 2004 -2025 (Two Decades in Review) ‎The report, however, points to growth in some non-traditional exports. ‎Cocoa products increased their share from 9.8 percent in 2004 to 27 percent in 2025, while edible fruits and nuts increased from 6.1 percent to 12.1 percent. ‎Plastics accounted for 8.5 percent of exports in 2025. ‎ Asia becomes Ghana’s biggest trading region ‎The report also highlights a major shift in Ghana’s trading relationships. ‎Asia accounted for 50.1 percent of Ghana’s exports in 2025, up from just 7.9 percent in 2004. ‎Over the same period, Europe’s share of exports fell from 51.2 percent to 26.8 percent. ‎Asia has also become Ghana’s largest source of imports, with its share increasing from 26.9 percent in 2004 to 48.4 percent in 2025. ‎Europe’s share of imports, meanwhile, declined from 45.9 percent to 24.7 percent. ‎ Fuel and vehicles remain major imports ‎On the import side, mineral fuels and oils accounted for 25.7 percent of imports in 2025. ‎Vehicles and automotive parts represented 15.4 percent, while machinery and electrical equipment accounted for 13.9 percent. ‎The GSS says the findings point to opportunities to strengthen domestic value addition, increase production and improve trade facilitation. ‎ GSS calls for greater value addition ‎The report recommends greater value addition in Ghana’s gold and cocoa industries, expansion of non-traditional exports and stronger support for small and medium-sized enterprises seeking to enter export markets. It also highlights the growing importance of Asian markets and the need for Ghanaian businesses to meet international market standards. ‎The statistics are based on customs records from the Ghana Revenue Authority’s Integrated Customs Management System (ICUMS) and follow United Nations International Merchandise Trade Statistics standards. ‎The GSS says the report is intended to support policy development, business decisions, research and public understanding of Ghana’s trade performance.

items.title: Osun election: I’ll give governance back to people — AAC candidate
items.description: The governorship candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC) in the Osun State governorship election, Olajide Esan, has pledged to return governance to the people if elected on August 15. Esan made the promise during the Arise Television town hall for governorship candidates ahead of Saturday’s election, where he outlined his plans for improving accountability and citizen participation in governance. The AAC candidate said Osun had suffered from a lack of genuine leadership despite having many politicians, arguing that leadership should be centred on service rather than the exploitation of the people’s challenges. “Osun state deficient of leadership. Even though we have too many politicians, but we don’t have leaders because leadership is all about service,” Esan said. He accused politicians of exploiting poverty and other challenges confronting the people, saying his administration would seek to reverse that pattern by giving residents a greater role in governance. “If I would be going into my vision, what is important to me is to give governance back to the people, because instead of leaders to be serving the people in Nigeria, especially in Osun State, it is the people who are serving the leaders,” he said. Esan said his administration would establish an Osun Resident Database to provide government with accurate information about residents and help in planning and delivering services. “Part of the plans we have, we have what I call Osun resident database. This database will give us the opportunity to have the information of Osun residents and to also be able to put the right things in place for Osun people,” he said. He also proposed a financial dashboard that would allow residents to monitor government spending and demand explanations where public funds were not properly accounted for. “Financial dashboard will give Osun people the opportunity to monitor and to track government spendings, so that if one error happens, they can call me that youth governor. Where is our one naira?” Esan said. According to him, greater transparency and accountability would discourage politicians from treating governance as a business venture. “Accountability is very important. Because the lack of accountability is what is making politics a lucrative business to career politicians,” he said. Esan added that the proposed measures would ensure that government became more responsive to residents and make it difficult for those seeking public office for personal gain to continue operating as usual. “Once these things are there, it will no longer be business as usual for those who actually want to serve the people,” he said. items.title: Última hora del terremoto en Colombia, en directo | Asciende a 224 la cifra de muertos por el seísmo en Colombia de magnitud 7,4
items.description: Al menos 224 personas han muerto y cientos han resultado heridas en Colombia por el terremoto de magnitud 7,4 que sacudió el oeste del país el lunes a las 7.34 de la mañana hora local (14.34, hora peninsular española), según las autoridades locales. El Servicio Geológico Colombiano ha registrado 47 réplicas hasta las 18:30 (1:30 de la madrugada del día siguiente, hora peninsular española). Desde este organismo advierten que “es probable” que se registren más. Aunque la magnitud máxima que han alcanzado es de 4,8, “baja comparada con el sismo principal”. El presidente colombiano, Abelardo de la Espriella, ha cifrado en 188 personas los desaparecidos en Cali y ha explicado que continúan las labores de búsqueda y rescate de los supervivientes durante la noche. Gran parte de los fallecidos se concentra en el área metropolitana de Pereira y también se han producido graves destrozos en la ciudad de Cali. items.title: Stakeholders urge sustained investment in youth to harness demographic dividend
items.description: Ghana must sustain investment in youth skills, reproductive health, and drug-abuse prevention to harness its demographic dividend, stakeholders have said. They said coordinated interventions were needed to address unemployment, population pressures, inadequate reproductive health services, and substance abuse, which could undermine the benefits of a growing youth population. A representative of the Regional Director of the National Youth Authority (NYA), William Nortey, made the call during activities to mark the 2026 World Population Day on the theme “Investing in Ghana’s Future through Healthy, Skilled, and Empowered Young People.” The event brought together representatives of the NYA, National Population Council (NPC), and Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) to examine challenges affecting young people and strategies for building a healthy, skilled, and productive population. Mr Nortey said the country’s future depended on a healthy and skilled youth population capable of creating employment and contributing meaningfully to national development. He said the NYA’s National Apprenticeship Programme was being implemented in 24 skill areas to equip young people with employable skills and reduce their dependence on government employment. Mr Nortey said the first phase of the programme, which started in October 2025 and was expected to end in September 2026, would provide trainees with start-up kits to establish their own businesses after completing their training. He said the NYA was also implementing programmes to promote healthy lifestyles among young people, including education on the dangers of substance abuse. Mr Nortey said empowering young people with skills and ideas would create a brighter future by enabling them to become productive and self-reliant. Acting Greater Accra Regional Population Officer of the NPC,Nana Ama Obuobi-Donkor, said population challenges in the Greater Accra Region required the active involvement of traditional authorities, community leaders, and other stakeholders. She identified unemployment, overcrowded classrooms, and inadequate access to reproductive health services as major challenges that could undermine efforts to harness the demographic dividend. Mrs Obuobi-Donkor said rapid migration into the Greater Accra Region was putting pressure on available employment opportunities, while overcrowding in some schools affected the quality of education and skills development. She called for improved access to reproductive health information and services for young people, noting that misconceptions about family planning continued to prevent some young people from seeking appropriate services. Mrs Obuobi-Donkor urged health workers to adopt a more accommodating and tolerant approach towards young people seeking reproductive health services, saying they should provide accurate information without making them feel unwelcome. She said the NPC integrated population variables into development planning from the national to regional and district levels to ensure that population dynamics informed policy and resource allocation. Senior Narcotics Control Officer of NACOC Sandra Thompson warned that substance abuse posed a serious threat to efforts to build a healthy and productive youth population. She said education and prevention were critical in addressing drug abuse among young people and cautioned against peer pressure, curiosity, and the misuse of substances, including shisha and prescription medicines. Mrs Thompson urged young people to make informed choices and resist influences that could expose them to substance abuse, saying the country’s demographic dividend could only be achieved when young people were healthy, skilled, and empowered.

items.title: Lahore hospitals report surge in gastroenteritis patients amid conflicting outbreak reports
items.description: LAHORE: Amid conflicting reports regarding the outbreak of gastroenteritis in the provincial capital, some hospitals witnessed an extraordinary rush of patients brought in with severe complications of the waterborne disease. The situation was said to be particularly alarming at the province’s largest teaching hospital, Mayo Hospital, where medics said they were receiving patients with complications including kidney failure and stroke. Other government hospitals, including Lahore General Hospital, Jinnah Hospital and Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, witnessed a spike in the number of patients, while the management of Services Hospital said its patient numbers were routine. “We are receiving a good number of patients with stomach infections, which may be the result of massive rains in the city,” said a spokesperson for Lahore General Hospital. Quoting a senior medical consultant at the hospital, the spokesperson said the majority of hospitalised patients were children. “We are receiving a large number of patients with gastroenteritis, many of them with kidney failure and stroke, which requires epidemiological investigation by public health experts,” said Dr Salman Kazmi, a senior medical consultant at Mayo Hospital, Lahore. He said that every medical unit of the hospital was facing a very unusual situation due to the long queues of patients with gastro infections. “I strongly believe that there may be an outbreak of cholera in the city, which has led to the extraordinary increase in the number of gastroenteritis patients,” he said. Dr Kazmi, who is also secretary-general of the Young Doctors Association Pakistan, added that cholera outbreaks usually occur as a sudden spike in severe diarrhoea and dehydration caused by Vibrio cholerae bacteria from contaminated water or food. Other contributing factors to a cholera outbreak include poor hygiene practices, unsafe drinking water and contaminated food. “Even the emergency ward of Mayo Hospital has witnessed a high influx of patients with stroke, low blood pressure and complications from diarrhoea,” Kazmi said. He said he could not comment on the official number of patients reported at the hospital due to faulty procedures in the data registration system. Services Hospital Lahore Principal Prof Zohra said that everything was normal in the medical units of her teaching institute, denying any outbreak of diarrhoea or gastroenteritis so far. Dr Mohammad Arshad, a former senior consultant at Shaikh Zayed Hospital, said that every year hospitals and clinics see a sharp rise in patients suffering from stomach infections, diarrhoea, vomiting and fever during the monsoon season . Most of these illnesses were caused by contaminated water and food, he said, adding that the city’s major hospitals had been facing a rush of patients with gastroenteritis for the past two weeks or so. Arshad said the illness might be a result of improper food storage, exposure to street food and unsafe drinking water, adding that health authorities must investigate the situation and take precautionary measures. He further said food businesses needed to exercise caution. Arshad added that unsafe drinking water and contaminated food could affect digestive health and increase the risk of stomach infections, gastrointestinal infections and food poisoning.

items.title: Crédit conso : la Banque d’Algérie exige un coup d’accélérateur
items.description: Après leur avoir fixé un délai de deux mois pour faciliter l’accès des ménages aux produits et services bancaires et abaissé le seuil des taux excessifs, la Banque d’Algérie est revenue à la charge pour exiger un coup d’accélérateur du crédit à la consommation « exclusivement » réservé aux produits « made in Algeria ». « Dans le cadre de la promotion du crédit à la consommation et du renforcement de son rôle dans le financement des besoins des ménages, les banques et les établissements financiers sont appelés à intensifier leurs efforts en vue de favoriser un accès plus large des ménages aux crédits à la consommation », a écrit le régulateur financier dans une note publiée lundi 10 août. Crédit à la consommation : la Banque d’Algérie exige de nouvelles offres Les banques et les établissements financiers algériens sont tenus de développer « davantage » leurs offres de crédit à la consommation, en « veillant à leur accessibilité » et à leur « adéquation » avec les besoins de la clientèle et à « assurer un traitement diligent des demandes de crédit, notamment en faisant appel aux canaux de distribution digitaux», selon cette note consultée par TSA. Pour accélérer le développement du crédit à la consommation, les banques doivent mobiliser les « moyens appropriés pour améliorer l’accès de leur clientèle à ce type de financement » qui est destiné « exclusivement à l’acquisition de biens produits ou assemblés en Algérie. » Les produits importés sont donc exclus du crédit à la consommation. Enfin, la Banque d’Algérie a demandé aux banques et aux établissements financiers de « prendre les mesures nécessaires » pour assurer la mise en œuvre de sa note, et de veiller à son « application effective, sans délai, au niveau de l’ensemble de leurs réseaux. » L’article Crédit conso : la Banque d’Algérie exige un coup d’accélérateur est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Dinguiraye : la mairie débloque plus de 20 millions GNF pour badigeonner les abords d’un pont : Des citoyens totalement hébétés
items.description: A Dinguiraye, une portion badigeonnée des abords d’un pont situé dans la commune urbaine suscite des interrogations sur les conditions dans lesquelles le marché a été attribué et financé. Et, le coût des « travaux » fait sérieusement jaser. Installé il y a un peu plus d’un mois, « le conseil communal a débloqué plus de 20 millions de francs guinéens pour cette opération, sans appel d’offres ». Une portion dudit pont a fait l’objet de « travaux de réfection » lundi 10 janvier, à l’initiative de la mairie. Si l’intervention vise à améliorer l’état de cette infrastructure et à faciliter la circulation des usagers, les conditions entourant son financement, le coût et l’attribution du marché soulèvent des préoccupations au sein de la population urbaine de Dinguiraye. Selon des informations recueillies sur place, plus de 20 millions de francs guinéens auraient été prélevés des caisses de la commune pour financer les travaux. Une dépense qui aurait été engagée alors que le conseil communal n’aurait pas suivi la procédure habituelle de passation des marchés publics. A en croire nos sources, aucun appel d’offres n’aurait été lancé pour sélectionner l’entreprise ou le prestataire chargé d’exécuter les travaux. Le marché aurait plutôt été attribué de gré à gré. Plus préoccupant encore, plusieurs conseillers communaux affirment ne pas avoir été informés du déblocage de cette somme et qu’aucune session n’a été tenue pour valider ou invalider le décaissement. La situation pose ainsi plusieurs questions sur la transparence de la gestion des ressources publiques au niveau de la mairie de Dinguiraye : dans quelles conditions la décision de financer ces travaux a-t-elle été prise ? Quel organe a autorisé le décaissement des fonds ? Pourquoi aucun appel d’offres n’a-t-il été lancé ? Et sur quelle base le marché a-t-il été attribué de gré à gré ? Pour l’heure, aucune explication officielle de la mairie de Dinguiraye n’a été portée à la connaissance du public concernant le montant exact engagé, l’entreprise bénéficiaire du marché, ainsi que les raisons ayant motivé le recours au gré à gré. Au-delà de la qualité des travaux réalisés, c’est donc la question de la transparence dans la gestion des ressources de la commune qui se retrouve au cœur des préoccupations. items.title: Birth Registration: 3.5m children ‘invisible’ in South-West, Edo records — Report
items.description: Every Nigerian child must be registered — UNICEF By Chioma Obinna & Rotimi Ojomoyela No fewer than 3.5 million children under one year across the six South-West states and Edo State have no birth registration, leaving them without legal identity and effectively “invisible” in government records, the United Nations Children’s Fund, UNICEF, has warned. UNICEF said the huge gap in birth registration could have serious consequences for the affected children, including difficulties accessing education, healthcare and social protection, as well as proving their age and nationality later in life. Chief, UNICEF Lagos Field Office, Celine Lafoucriere, who disclosed this at a two-day media dialogue on birth registration of children under one year, organised by the Lagos State Office of the National Population Commission, NPC, in collaboration with UNICEF, said every child had a fundamental right to legal identity. “Every single child in Nigeria should be registered. This is the foundational first right of a child. Every single Nigerian child needs to be registered in Nigeria,” she said. Lafoucriere said the estimated 3.5 million unregistered children across the region represented more than a statistics gap, warning that children not captured in the civil register could also be left out when government plans and funds social programmes. She said: “If 3.5 million children are still not registered, they will go unnoticed and there will be no government funding to support them simply because they are invisible.” The UNICEF official explained that birth registration was not merely about obtaining a certificate but about formally establishing a child’s existence before the law. According to her, an unregistered child could encounter difficulties accessing basic services and exercising rights throughout life. “They do not exist for access to basic social services like education, like health. But they will also continue not to exist as they reach adult age when it is time for them to vote, to participate in political life, but also when they will be in a position to inherit their parents’ wealth. “As they are not registered, they are invisible,” she said. Lafoucriere identified inadequate awareness, geographical isolation, limited access to registration points and gaps in the digital registration system among factors responsible for the persistent registration deficit. She said many parents were unaware that birth registration was free or that registration could be completed at health facilities and community-level registration points. “Some parents are very willing to do so but it remains difficult in some geographical contexts,” she said. According to her, UNICEF is supporting government efforts to digitalise birth registration and take the service closer to families, particularly those in underserved communities. She urged the media to intensify public enlightenment and tell the stories of children and families affected by the registration gap. The UNICEF official also stressed that accurate civil registration was essential to the development of an effective social protection system. She explained that government could only adequately plan and allocate resources when it knew how many children required services. “If we are working, and the government is working on building a social protection system, having a civil register is very important. But in that civil register, no child that is not registered at birth will exist,” she said. Lafoucriere, however, noted that progress had been made, particularly with efforts to link birth registration to the National Identification Number, NIN, saying the development would strengthen children’s legal identity from birth. In his welcome address, Lagos State Director of the National Population Commission, Abiola Kekere-Ekun, urged the media to move beyond reporting statistics and government activities and take the birth registration message directly to parents and caregivers. He said reliable birth registration data was crucial for effective governance because it enabled government to determine the number and distribution of children and plan adequately for education, healthcare, social protection and other services. Also speaking, UNICEF Child Protection Specialist, Denis Onoise, said about 24.8 million children under five had been registered across Nigeria. He described birth registration as a critical component of children’s rights because it provides legal recognition of a child’s existence. Onoise warned that children without birth certificates or recognised documentation could face serious difficulties proving their identity or age and accessing certain services later in life. He called for stronger public awareness and improved access to registration services, urging parents and caregivers to register children as early as possible. UNICEF Communication Officer, Blessing Ejiofor, said the media dialogue was aimed at strengthening journalists’ capacity to report effectively on birth registration and support advocacy for increased registration within the first year of life. She said universal birth registration would require sustained media advocacy, stronger coordination among relevant institutions, improved accessibility of registration services and accountability by authorities. The two-day dialogue brought together journalists from Lagos, Ogun, Osun, Ondo, Ekiti and Edo states, as well as representatives of government agencies, UNICEF, health workers and other stakeholders. items.title: GBA’s position on lawyers’ appearance before vacation Courts has ‘no legal basis’ – Deputy AG
items.description: Deputy Attorney-General and Minister for Justice, Justice Srem-Sai, has rejected the Ghana Bar Association’s position on proceedings during the legal vacation, insisting that lawyers have no legal basis to decide whether cases should be heard before Vacation Courts. He described the GBA’s position as “completely wrong”, arguing that it is unsupported by law, fact, reason or established rules of court practice. Justice Srem-Sai was responding to concerns raised by the GBA over directives requiring lawyers to appear before judges sitting during the current legal vacation. “There is no genuine or real controversy here,” he said. “The matter is simple. It’s been the case that vacation courts are always sitting whenever there’s a legal vacation. No one can dispute that simple fact.” The dispute follows a letter dated August 10, 2026, signed by GBA President Efua Ghartey and National Secretary Kwaku Gyau Baffour. The letter responded to petitions from the law firms Zoe, Akyea & Co, Dame & Partners, and Sam Okudzeto & Associates, which raised concerns over directives requiring them to appear before judges during the legal vacation. The GBA cited Order 79, Rule 4 of the High Court (Civil Procedure) Rules, 2004, CI 47, which provides for three annual legal vacations, including the longest vacation from August 1 to September 30. The association maintained that Vacation Courts traditionally deal with emergencies and interlocutory matters rather than trials. It also argued that the willingness and availability of counsel have traditionally been an important consideration in determining whether proceedings should take place during the vacation. Justice Srem-Sai, however, disagrees. According to the Deputy Attorney-General, the Chief Justice has issued warrants authorising about 10 or more judges across the country to sit during the legal vacation and deal with pending cases. He said those judges retain the authority to administer their courts and hear cases during the vacation period. “The claim that it is the lawyers who decide whether they want to have proceedings in vacation is not founded on any fact, is not founded on any law, is not founded on reason, and it is not founded by any rule of practice,” he said. “Lawyers nowhere in the world — you see lawyers telling when a court should sit.” Justice Srem-Sai said accepting the GBA’s interpretation could create significant delays in the administration of justice. He explained that judges assigned to Vacation Courts would ordinarily take their own leave after the legal vacation ends, potentially creating further periods during which trials could not proceed. “If you make the argument as the GBA president is making that a vacation judge is not required to or cannot hear cases or conduct trial, then when the vacation is over and he goes on vacation, no other judge can have trial,” he said. He argued that such an interpretation could mean some cases would not resume until January 2027. “Basically what the GBA is saying is that for cases that are pending in the courts that have vacation judges, those cases can only conduct trials in January next year,” he added. Justice Srem-Sai also rejected the GBA’s assertion that there is an established convention limiting the nature of proceedings that may be conducted during the legal vacation. “The claim that there is a convention is completely false. There’s no such convention,” he said. He argued that the relevant legal framework is Order 79 of CI 47, which expressly provides for legal vacation. The Deputy Attorney-General described the GBA’s interpretation as a “self-imposed understanding of the law” that should not be allowed to determine the administration of cases before the courts. Justice Srem-Sai further warned that lawyers who refuse to appear before Vacation Courts could expose their clients to serious consequences. He said judges who have been authorised to sit during the vacation are entitled to proceed with cases even when counsel fails to appear. “As the judge said, he has a warrant to hear the case and sit in vacation. And if you don’t come, he will treat it as if you are not interested in legal representation,” he said. According to him, affected clients have been given the opportunity to secure alternative legal representation if their lawyers decline to participate. He said where a lawyer fails to appear at the next adjourned date, the court could require the client to proceed without counsel. “If their lawyers decide that they won’t practice, no one can stop them, but he has a case to defend,” he said. “If on the next adjourn date, he does not produce a lawyer — the judge has given them one week. If they do not produce a lawyer, then they will have to conduct the cross-examination by themselves.”

items.title: Nayala: le ministre de la Santé encourage le personnel soignant, le BIR 23 et salue la résilience communautaire
items.description: BURKINA-NAYALA-VISITE-MINISTRE-SANTE Nayala: le ministre de la Santé encourage le personnel soignant, le BIR 23 et salue la résilience communautaire Toma, 10 août 2026 (AIB) – Le ministre de la Santé, Dr Robert Lucien Jean-Claude Kargougou, a effectué lundi une visite dans la province du Nayala, au cours de laquelle il s’est rendu au Centre médical avec antenne chirurgicale (CMA) de Toma, à la base du 23e Bataillon d’intervention rapide (BIR 23) et au Centre de santé et de promotion sociale (CSPS) de Koin pour encourager le personnel soignant et les forces combattantes et saluer la résilience des communautés. Accueilli par le haut-commissaire de la province du Nayala Honoré Frédéric Paré, ainsi que par les autorités administratives, coutumières, religieuses et les mouvements de veille citoyenne, le ministre a débuté sa visite au CMA de Toma. Il a visité les services des urgences, de la pédiatrie, du laboratoire, de la maternité et du bloc opératoire. Les échanges avec le médecin-chef du district, Dr Constantin Sow, et le personnel soignant ont permis de relever la vétusté des équipements médico-techniques, les besoins en personnel ainsi que les difficultés administratives rencontrées par les agents. Le ministre a salué l’engagement du personnel soignant dans un contexte sécuritaire difficile. Il a réaffirmé le caractère stratégique de la santé pour le président du Faso et annoncé des mesures visant à accélérer le traitement de plusieurs dossiers administratifs des agents de santé de Toma avant la fin de l’année. À la base du BIR 23, le ministre a rendu hommage aux forces combattantes pour leur engagement. Il a souligné que leur action contribue à assurer la circulation des personnes, des vaccins et des médicaments, ainsi que la continuité des services essentiels de santé. Il les a exhortées à maintenir leur détermination dans la reconquête du territoire national. La délégation s’est ensuite rendue au CSPS de Koin, où elle a constaté les efforts consentis par la communauté pour améliorer les infrastructures sanitaires, notamment à travers des aménagements locaux et l’équipement du centre. Le ministre a félicité les populations pour cette mobilisation et assuré que les services techniques compétents examineront les problèmes d’inondation qui affectent les locaux du CSPS. Cette visite renforce les attentes des acteurs locaux concernant l’équipement progressif du CMA de Toma, afin de lui permettre de répondre pleinement aux normes sanitaires et aux besoins des populations du Nayala. items.title: Effondrement d’un immeuble à Hafia, 5 morts : « le gouvernement est là pour la population », assure le ministre Sy Savané
items.description: Le ministre de l’Urbanisme, de l’Habitat et de l’Aménagement du territoire, Mohamed Lamine Sy Savané, s’est rendu à Hafia 1, où un immeuble R+5 en construction s’est effondré sur une villa, faisant cinq morts. Screenshot " data-large-file="https://i0.wp.com/mediaguinee.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/IMG_6679.jpeg?fit=1024%2C756&ssl=1" class="wp-image-323107 size-full" src="https://i0.wp.com/mediaguinee.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/IMG_6679.jpeg?resize=1170%2C864&ssl=1" alt="" width="1170" height="864" srcset="https://i0.wp.com/mediaguinee.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/IMG_6679.jpeg?w=1787&ssl=1 1787w, https://i0.wp.com/mediaguinee.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/IMG_6679.jpeg?resize=300%2C222&ssl=1 300w, https://i0.wp.com/mediaguinee.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/IMG_6679.jpeg?resize=1024%2C756&ssl=1 1024w, https://i0.wp.com/mediaguinee.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/IMG_6679.jpeg?resize=768%2C567&ssl=1 768w, https://i0.wp.com/mediaguinee.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/IMG_6679.jpeg?resize=1536%2C1135&ssl=1 1536w, https://i0.wp.com/mediaguinee.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/IMG_6679.jpeg?resize=86%2C64&ssl=1 86w" sizes="(max-width: 1170px) 100vw, 1170px" /> Screenshot Sur les lieux, le ministre a présenté ses condoléances aux familles endeuillées ainsi que celles des plus hautes autorités du pays. Dans sa communication, Mohamed Lamine Sy Savané a indiqué que l’Agence nationale de gestion des urgences et catastrophes (ANGUCH), l’administration du territoire ainsi que les services compétents du ministère de l’Habitat se sont mobilisés pour porter secours aux victimes. « Nous avons réussi à extraire 9 personnes. Nous avons enregistré 4 morts malheureusement. Nous gardons l’espoir qu’à la fin de la fouille, nous allons retrouver d’autres survivants », a-t-il déclaré. Le ministre a également exhorté les populations de Conakry, mais aussi celles de l’intérieur du pays, à faire preuve de davantage de vigilance. « Pour ceux qui ont suivi, les services compétents, conformément au communiqué du gouvernement qui suspendait tous les travaux dans le Grand Conakry et dans les autres grandes villes, ce chantier a connu malheureusement une reprise hier. Comme pour répondre, l’effondrement s’en est suivi », a-t-il déploré. Selon le ministre, les populations riveraines avaient été informées et alertées sur les risques liés au site. « Les populations riveraines, je vais parler des citoyens qui sont autour de l’immeuble, ont été informées, alertées sur le lieu. Très malheureusement, certains ont respecté, d’autres, comme la famille, sont malheureusement venus la nuit s’abriter. Encore, le drame a endeuillé une personne. Une personne perdue est de trop », a-t-il regretté. Mohamed Lamine Sy Savané a par ailleurs rassuré les Guinéens quant à la mobilisation des autorités face à ce drame. « Le gouvernement est là pour la population. Madame la ministre en charge de l’Administration du territoire, qui venait de prendre la haute responsabilité de ce département stratégique, et les autres départements tels que la Sécurité, l’Habitat, l’Environnement, naturellement, le ministère de la Défense, nous allons travailler, prendre en charge les conclusions des différents rapports », a-t-il assuré. Pour finir, le ministre a une nouvelle fois appelé les citoyens à respecter les instructions et les consignes des services compétents. « Je demande encore une fois à tous nos concitoyens de respecter les instructions, les communiqués et les consignes données par les services compétents », a-t-il conclu. Mamadou Yaya BARRY L’article Effondrement d’un immeuble à Hafia, 5 morts : « le gouvernement est là pour la population », assure le ministre Sy Savané est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Specialised courts sitting during legal vacation novel – Joseph Kpempa
items.description: Joseph Kpempa, lead counsel for former National Petroleum Authority (NPA) Chief Executive Officer, Dr Mustapha Abdul-Hamid, has described the decision to continue proceedings during the legal vacation as novel. The comments follow a decision by the Accra High Court to reject a request by lawyers for four accused persons to adjourn the trial until October when the legal vacation ends. The defence teams had asked the court to suspend proceedings for the vacation, citing personal commitments and the usual practice of courts during the period. However, the court declined the request and directed that the trial should continue during the legal vacation. The judge indicated that proceedings would continue unless the Chief Justice, Paul Baffoe-Bonnie, withdraws the warrant directing selected high-profile criminal cases to proceed during the vacation. Reacting to the development, the lawyer said the directive was unusual, particularly because courts traditionally deal with urgent applications and interlocutory matters during the legal vacation rather than substantive trials. According to him, the Chief Justice has the discretion under the Courts Act to make arrangements for courts to sit during weekends, holidays and other periods when necessary. However, he said the current arrangement was different because two specialised courts had been directed to conduct substantive criminal trials during the vacation. “It is novel. We’ve not done that,” he said. He explained that there was often confusion between the work of vacation courts and substantive hearings. “During the holidays, judges do not normally deal with the substantive hearings. It is only motions. The holiday judges sit to hear motions and urgent applications,” he noted. The lawyer argued that the decision to have the specialised courts continue with normal trial proceedings during the vacation therefore represents a departure from established practice. “If you look at the two specialised courts, they are asked to do normal hearings that we do during the normal period that we are in court, as against the vacation,” he said. The development means the trial involving Dr Abdul-Hamid and his co-accused will proceed despite the defence’s request for an adjournment until October. The former NPA boss and other accused persons are facing charges including extortion and related offences in connection with allegations involving players in Ghana’s petroleum sector. The Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) alleges that Dr Abdul-Hamid and others unlawfully obtained money from bulk oil transporters and oil marketing companies. The accused persons have denied the allegations and are contesting the charges. The case has been listed among a number of high-profile criminal matters designated to continue during the legal vacation.
