items.title: Republic Bank Ghana, JoyNews launch 2026 Habitat Fair
items.description: Republic Bank Ghana and JoyNews, a member of the Multimedia Group Limited, have launched the 2026 Habitat Fair, with Republic Bank coming on board as the lead sponsor. The JoyNews Habitat Fair is an annual housing and lifestyle exhibition that brings together stakeholders across Ghana’s housing sector, including financial institutions, developers, homeowners and service providers. Speaking at the launch, Manager in charge of Mortgages at Republic Bank Ghana, Frank Oppong Yeboah, advised prospective homeowners to build according to their income and financial capacity rather than take on excessive debt to complete expensive homes at once. “You don’t just go about taking a loan and developing a four-bedroom, two-storey house,” he said. “You can decide to have one bedroom, living and dining, with all the facilities, and then as you progress, or as your income increases, you add on,” he added. Mr Yeboah said a gradual approach to homeownership could help individuals avoid placing unnecessary pressure on their finances. Managing Director of Republic Bank Ghana, Dr Benjamin Dzoboku, also identified affordability as one of the biggest challenges confronting Ghana’s housing sector. According to him, the challenge goes beyond the availability of housing units, particularly as population growth and urbanisation continue to increase demand. “The challenge is not the supply side, but affordability,” he said. Dr Dzoboku noted that Ghana’s housing deficit, estimated at 1.8 million units in 2015, had been compounded by rapid population growth and urbanisation. He said addressing the housing gap would require stronger collaboration among government, financial institutions, developers and other stakeholders in the sector. “Closing this gap will require a concerted effort, not only from one institution or two institutions, but all stakeholders,” he stressed. General Manager of Joy Brands at Multimedia Group Limited, Francis Fiifi Koomson, welcomed the partnership and expressed confidence that it would contribute positively to Ghana’s housing industry while creating opportunities for both organisations. As part of the launch, Multimedia Group’s General Manager for Sales, David Max-Fugar, signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Republic Bank Ghana to formalise the partnership. The partnership is expected to support activities leading to this year’s Habitat Fair later in 2026.

items.title: Publicités frauduleuses: Meta sanctionné pour avoir détruit des preuves
items.description: Un juge fédéral californien a sanctionné lundi Meta pour avoir détruit des preuves dans l'affaire l'opposant au milliardaire australien, Andrew Forrest, qui accuse la maison mère de Facebook d'avoir laissé prospérer des publicités frauduleuses utilisant son image pour promouvoir de faux investissements en cryptomonnaies. Obtenir la reconnaissance que Meta est responsable de la disparition de ces preuves est au cœur de la stratégie du célèbre magnat minier: ce dernier cherche à démontrer devant la justice que Meta modifie activement les publicités qu'il diffuse sur ses réseaux sociaux et peut donc être tenu responsable de leur contenu frauduleux. En face, Meta s'abrite derrière un bouclier juridique au cœur de la plupart des batailles judiciaires contre les géants de la tech depuis trente ans: la Section 230 d'une loi américaine de 1996 qui exonère les plateformes de responsabilité pour les contenus publiés chez elles par des tiers. Dans sa décision, consultée par l'AFP, le juge P. Casey Pitts estime que le groupe de Menlo Park (Californie) a bien détruit ou laissé s'effacer des données essentielles, causant un préjudice au plaignant. Meta affirmait avoir eu besoin de deux ans pour découvrir l'existence de ces données dans ses propres systèmes, ce qui n'est « tout simplement pas crédible », balaye le magistrat. Meta soutenait aussi n'avoir jamais détenu les publicités telles qu'affichées aux utilisateurs, celles-ci étant assemblées sur leurs téléphones ou ordinateurs. Le magistrat écarte cet argument en invoquant les déclarations d'un ingénieur du groupe: Meta « aurait pu conserver ces données mais a choisi de ne pas le faire ». Le juge n'a toutefois pas retenu l'intention de nuire, préférant qualifier le comportement du groupe de « négligence grave ». Si l'affaire va jusqu'au procès, il reviendra au jury de trancher cette question. Mais avant cela, Meta peut encore tenter de faire rejeter l'affaire en plaidant que son immunité s'applique toujours et le protège d'un procès, ce que le juge Pitts devra trancher seul, sans jury. Cette affaire s'inscrit dans une série de revers judiciaires pour Meta. Le 10 avril, la Cour suprême du Massachusetts a jugé que la Section 230 ne protégeait pas le groupe des poursuites liées à la conception d'Instagram. En mars, des jurés de Santa Fe (Nouveau-Mexique) et de Los Angeles l'ont jugé responsable des effets de ses plateformes sur les mineurs. Dans tous ces dossiers, les plaignants contournent le bouclier de la même manière : ils n'attaquent pas ce que les utilisateurs publient, mais la façon dont les plateformes le mettent en avant et paramètrent leurs applications. Un nouveau procès sur ce fondement s'ouvre mercredi à Oakland (Californie), où quatre États réclament à Meta jusqu'à 1.400 milliards de dollars pour la mise en danger des mineurs. The post Publicités frauduleuses: Meta sanctionné pour avoir détruit des preuves appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Ouaga | Lutte antivectorielle : La mairie de l’arrondissement 9 mobilise les populations de quatre secteurs pour éliminer les gîtes larvaires
items.description: La Présidente de la Délégation Spéciale de l’arrondissement 9 de Ouagadougou a appelé les habitants des secteurs 37, 38, 39 et 40 à une mobilisation citoyenne, dans le cadre des Journées nationales de lutte antivectorielle. Selon le communiqué de la mairie, des activités de salubrité sont organisées pour éliminer les gîtes larvaires, ces lieux favorisant la reproduction des moustiques vecteurs de maladies comme le paludisme. Cette initiative du Gouvernement burkinabè, lancée le 8 août 2026, vise à débarrasser les milieux de vie des objets pouvant retenir l’eau. La mairie invite la population à participer activement à la collecte et au dépôtage des déchets, notamment tout objet creux tel que les pneus usagés. Pour cela, quatre sites ont été identifiés pour la destruction des déchets. Il s’agit du Centre de Collecte et de Tri situé sur la voie de Gambd-yaar, à environ deux kilomètres du Commissariat de Police de l’arrondissement 9, au secteur 37. Également, la carrière située derrière le château d'eau ONEA de Nonghin, à environ deux kilomètres du siège de la Mairie, au secteur 38. La place publique située à environ deux mètres du portail 22, au secteur 39, est également retenue. Enfin, la carrière située à proximité de la Mosquée de vendredi en bordure de la Route Nationale 22 menant vers Petit Ouaga, au secteur 40. La Présidente de la délégation spéciale, par l’intermédiaire du Secrétaire Général Arzouma Jedn Ludovic Sorgho, compte sur l'engagement de tous pour une lutte efficace contre les maladies vectorielles. Cette opération de terrain s’inscrit dans une stratégie de prévention qui passe par l’assainissement et la suppression des eaux stagnantes, comme le rappellent les autorités sanitaires dans le cadre de cette journée nationale. items.title: Republic Bank becomes title sponsor of JoyNews Habitat Fair
items.description: Republic Bank Ghana has become the new title sponsor of the JoyNews Habitat Fair, following the signing of a three-year partnership agreement with the Multimedia Group Limited. The agreement, signed at the headquarters of Republic Bank in Accra on Tuesday, August 11, 2026, covers all Habitat Fair events across Multimedia Group brands and locations nationwide. The partnership builds on an existing relationship between Republic Bank and the Multimedia Group, with the bank having served as title sponsor of the Habitat Fair organised by Luv FM in Kumasi for the past three years. Fiifi Koomson, General Manager of Joy Brands at Multimedia Group, said the success of the Kumasi collaboration made the expansion a natural next step. “Three years ago, Republic Bank became the title sponsor of the Habitat Fair of Kumasi brands, Luv FM. That was a very exciting time, and we’ve had a very exciting journey,” he said. Mr Koomson described the new agreement as a “statement of confidence” in the Multimedia Group, adding that the Accra brands are covered for an initial three years. Making homeownership achievable Managing Director of Republic Bank Ghana, Dr Benjamin Dzoboku, said the partnership comes at a time when Ghana continues to grapple with a significant housing deficit, with affordability remaining one of the biggest obstacles to homeownership. He noted that Ghana’s housing deficit was estimated at about 1.8 million housing units in 2015, with rapid urbanisation and population growth continuing to widen the gap. According to him, the challenge goes beyond the availability of housing units. “The challenge is not the supply side but affordability,” he said, citing low household incomes, borrowing costs and land litigation among the major barriers confronting prospective homeowners. Dr Dzoboku stressed that addressing Ghana’s housing challenge would require a concerted effort involving government, financial institutions, developers, the media and other stakeholders. Housing finance in Republic Bank’s DNA He said housing finance has been central to Republic Bank’s identity since its origins as a home finance company in 1990. “Republic Bank financing of housing, as you all know, is not a side business. It is part of our gene,” he said. The bank, he explained, has evolved from a mortgage-focused home finance company into a commercial bank, but has retained its expertise and commitment to helping Ghanaians achieve their homeownership ambitions. Range of home financing options Dr Dzoboku said Republic Bank currently offers a range of products designed to support customers at different stages of the homeownership journey. These include financing for buying, building and owning a home, home completion and improvement, home equity financing, pension-backed mortgages and other housing finance solutions. He also highlighted the bank’s involvement in the National Housing Scheme with the government, through which it has supported public sector workers to acquire homes. Beyond homeownership, he said Republic Bank had also established a Real Estate Investment Fund in 1995, providing an avenue for people interested in investing in the real estate sector. He described the bank’s approach to housing as an ecosystem that enables Ghanaians to save, invest, build, buy and create security for their families. Habitat Fair goes nationwide Dr Dzoboku welcomed the expansion of the Habitat Fair partnership beyond Accra and Kumasi to give more Ghanaians access to information and opportunities around housing. He said the national reach would allow people in different parts of the country to engage financial institutions, developers and other players in the housing sector. “So if you are a nurse in Accra, or a teacher in Zebila, or an entrepreneur in Ho, you can also have your dream home through this fair,” he said. He encouraged prospective homeowners not to abandon their aspirations because of financial or other challenges. “Do not abandon your dream of owning a home. Come to Republic Bank Ghana. Let us understand your circumstances. We have various options and we can chart the right path for you,” he said. He described the Habitat Fair as an important platform for stakeholders in the housing ecosystem to engage directly with prospective homeowners, answer their questions and provide practical solutions. Habitat Fair expands to Ho General Manager, Sales at the Multimedia Group, Max Fugar, who signed the agreement on behalf of the company, described the development as a return of the Habitat Fair “home” under a new national partnership with Republic Bank. He announced that the Habitat Fair will be held in Accra, Kumasi and Ho, expanding its reach to the Volta Region this year. “Joy News Habitat Fair is back home. Republic Bank is now the lead sponsor of Joy News Habitat Fair. Accra, Kumasi, and Ho,” Mr Fugar said. He expressed appreciation to Republic Bank for its support and assured the bank that the Multimedia Group would deliver on the partnership. Habitat Fair Clinic to begin at Achimota Mall As part of activities leading to the main fair, Mr Fugar announced that the Habitat Fair Clinic will be held at Achimota Mall from August 21 to 23. The clinic will provide an opportunity for prospective homeowners to engage directly with exhibitors and experts, including Republic Bank, on financing and other aspects of homeownership. He encouraged members of the public to take advantage of the clinic and subsequent engagements across Multimedia Group platforms to seek answers to their housing and financing questions. The signing ceremony was broadcast live on Joy FM and Joy News, as well as the organisation’s digital platforms. The partnership between Republic Bank and the Multimedia Group is expected to strengthen the Habitat Fair as a platform connecting prospective homeowners with financial institutions, developers, construction companies and other players across Ghana’s housing ecosystem.

Salary hike: Tinubu should ensure direct transfer for military – Ndume
items.description: By John Alechenu Former Senate Leader, Ali Ndume, has commended President Bola Tinubu for approving salary increases for about 250,000 personnel of the Nigerian Armed Forces, saying the move will go a long way to boost the morale of troops. President Tinubu last week approved salary increases of between 30 and 80 per cent for military personnel. The new rates take effect next month. With the adjustment, the annual wage bill for the Armed Forces will rise from N660 billion to N924 billion. Officers above the rank of colonel -brigadier-generals, major-generals, lieutenant-generals and generals – will get 30 per cent increase. Those from colonel down to warrant officer will get 50 per cent, while personnel from private to staff sergeant will get 80 per cent. In a statement in Abuja on Tuesday, Ndume, who once chaired the Senate Committee on Army, said the salary review shows the President has a clear plan to tackle insecurity. He said, “This coming after his recent expansion of military divisions from eight to 12 shows that Mr. President has his own blueprint aimed at dealing with the scourge of terrorism and banditry. “The review of salary will go a long way in motivating our military personnel. I have been in the vanguard of better motivation for our men and officers in the military in terms of decent living wage. “President Tinubu has once again proved that he is a responsive leader who doesn’t shut his mind to genuine and legitimate agitation of Nigerians.” However, the Borno South Senator noted that better pay alone will not win the war against insurgency. He urged the government to also ensure prompt supply of arms, ammunition and other logistics. Ndume said, “I have always argued that aside better welfare package and training, what they need to deal with insurgents is prompt supply of arms and ammunition. “I also want to urge Mr. President to keep up his pledge on the provision of weapons and technological tools required to the Armed Forces to effectively discharge their duties.” The APC Chieftain called for the annual defence budget to be placed on First Line Charge to remove bureaucratic delays. According to him, “All these can be achieved seamlessly if we put their annual budget on First Line Charge. This envelope budgeting is trapped in unnecessary bureaucracy between the Ministry of Defense and Ministry of Finance. It is a big encumbrance to effective operations of our men and officers in the war theater. “Mr. President should seize the initiative to ensure direct statutory transfer from the Federation Account for the military as it is done with few agencies of government.” The post Salary hike: Tinubu should ensure direct transfer for military – Ndume appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kloto/Eau et assainissement : Les acteurs locaux se concertent pour améliorer la gouvernance
items.description: Kpalimé, 11 août (ATOP) – Les acteurs locaux impliqués dans la gestion de l’eau et de l’assainissement dans la commune Kloto 1 ont échangé sur des défis liés à l’accès à l’eau potable, à la protection des ressources hydriques et à l’assainissement, le lundi 10 août à Kpalimé. Cette rencontre s’intègre dans le cadre de la Journée africaine de la décentralisation et du développement local (JADDL) 2026. Les acteurs ont échangé sur des solutions concertées pour un territoire plus sain, résilient et durable. L’état des lieux sur l’accès à l’eau potable et à l’assainissement dans la commune ainsi que sur le rôle des collectivités territoriales dans la gouvernance de ces secteurs a été présenté. Les discussions ont porté sur le thème local : « Gouvernance locale, accès à l’eau potable et assainissement : quels défis et quelles solutions pour la commune de Kloto 1 ? ». La qualité de l’eau a constitué l’une des principales préoccupations soulevées au cours des travaux. La protection des cours d’eau et de leurs berges, ainsi que la lutte contre les pratiques et produits susceptibles de polluer les ressources hydriques, ont également été abordées. Au terme des échanges, plusieurs recommandations ont été formulées en vue d’orienter les prochaines actions communales et du cadre permanent de dialogue entre les différents acteurs. Le 1 er adjoint au maire de Kloto 1, Nyawuame Eugène, a fait savoir que cette rencontre offre l’opportunité de mobiliser les différents acteurs autour des difficultés auxquelles sont confrontées les populations. « C’est ensemble que nous devons réfléchir pour que nos populations aient accès à l’eau potable et que notre environnement soit assaini », a-t-il déclaré. Pour Jacques Gaba, du Cadre de concertation pour l’assainissement de base au Togo, la célébration de la JADDL doit surtout favoriser le passage de la réflexion à l’action. Il a déclaré que la mobilisation des différents acteurs autour d’une gouvernance partagée de l’eau, constitue un levier pour relever les défis auxquels la commune est confrontée, afin de renforcer sa résilience. L ’édition 2026 de la JADDL est placée sous le thème « Autonomisation des Autorités locales pour une eau et un assainissement durable : faire progresser des villes et territoires résilients, inclusifs et durables vers l’Agenda 2063 ». Elle s’inscrit dans la dynamique des Objectifs de développement durable (ODD), notamment l’ODD 6 consacré à l’accès universel à l’eau potable et à l’assainissement. ATOP/AYH/AO/BV

items.title: Prof Bokpin warns against political recruitment into civil service
items.description: Economist and Professor of Finance Godfred Bokpin has cautioned against political recruitment into Ghana’s civil service, describing the practice as a dangerous development that could undermine effective governance and national development. Prof Bokpin acknowledged the critical role of the Civil Service in nation-building, stressing that it remained an essential institution for supporting continuity, professionalism and effective public administration. “The civil service plays an important role in assisting the government in formulating, implementing, monitoring and evaluating policies for national development,” he said. “In an increasingly polarised nation, divided along political lines, what becomes the balancing act and moderating element should be the civil service,” he added. However, he warned that politicising the service through the recruitment of individuals based on political considerations should not be tolerated. He described political recruitment into the Civil Service as a “poisonous” practice that could weaken the institution and compromise its ability to serve the national interest. “Your (Civil Servants) objectivity will be key. For that reason, we should not allow politics to influence recruitment into the public service and the civil service. It is one poison you don’t need to be advised to take,” he warned. “An inefficient civil service within the broader perspective of public service represents a cost to the private sector as they interact,” he added. Prof Bokpin made the remarks at a public lecture organised by the Office of the Head of the Civil Service on Tuesday, August 11, on the theme: “The Resetting Agenda for Sustainable Development in Ghana: The Civil Service’s Responsibilities.”

items.title: ECOWAS to offer $65,000 to Nigerian startups — How to apply
items.description: The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) has opened applications for its 2026 Startup Awards, with a total cash prize of $65,000 up for grabs among the top three startups. The second edition of the ECOWAS Startup Awards is designed to identify, celebrate and support high-impact startups contributing to digital transformation, regional integration and sustainable value-chain development across West Africa. The programme is being convened by the ECOWAS Commission’s Directorate of Private Sector and Industry, hosted in Abuja and jointly implemented by the Pan African Alliance of Small and Medium Industries (PAOSMI) and the Investment Promotion Agencies of West African States (IPAWAS). The initiative follows the inaugural edition held in Niamey, Niger, on November 18 and 19, 2021. The 2026 edition is expected to bring together 60 startups from ECOWAS Member States and will feature masterclasses, startup clinics, pitch competitions, exhibitions, investor deal rooms, policy dialogues and post-award acceleration. How much can startups win? The competition has a total cash prize of $65,000, divided among the top three startups. Winner — $30,000 First runner-up — $20,000 Second runner-up — $15,000 Beyond the cash prizes, selected startups will receive regional exposure across the ECOWAS bloc, investor introductions, networking opportunities with founders and policymakers, mentorship and a six-month acceleration programme. They will also have access to digital tools, including computers, accessories and software. Six sectors eligible for the awards Applications are open to startups operating in six strategic sectors: 1. EdTech Startups focused on education technology and skills development. 2. FinTech Businesses developing technology-driven financial products and services. 3. HealthTech Startups using technology to improve healthcare delivery and related services. 4. AgriTech Businesses working in agricultural technology and food systems. 5. CleanTech Startups focused on clean technology, climate solutions and green innovation. 6. TravelTech Businesses operating in tourism, hospitality and travel technology. Who can apply? Applicants must meet six eligibility requirements to participate in the competition. They must: Be a citizen of an ECOWAS Member State. Operate a startup that is registered and based within an ECOWAS country. Have been operating for at least two years. Have a working product or service. Demonstrate market traction or scalability. Submit all required documentation. What documents are required? Applicants are expected to prepare the following documents and materials before beginning the application: A completed application form covering Sections A–J. A national passport or ECOWAS-approved identity document for the lead founder, in PDF or image format and not exceeding 10MB. A recent colour passport photograph of not more than 5MB. Business registration certificate issued in an ECOWAS Member State, where applicable. Two years of financial statements, management accounts or projections. A business plan of no more than 10 pages, single-spaced and written in Times New Roman, size 12. A pitch deck of no more than 10 slides. A one-minute pitch video in MP4, MOV or WebM format, with a maximum file size of 100MB. How will startups be selected? The selection process will take place in two phases. National selection Each ECOWAS Member State will nominate half of its allocated slots. The remaining half will be selected from applications submitted by the general public, meaning startups do not necessarily need a national nomination to secure a place in the competition. Regional finals Selected finalists will pitch before an independent regional jury in Abuja. Winners will be determined based on scoring and consensus, with judges drawn from industry, investment and policy backgrounds. The organisers said judges will be required to comply with conflict-of-interest and confidentiality policies. Important dates The application portal opened on August 3, 2026, and interested startups have until August 31, 2026, to submit their applications. The programme will then move into its next stages: August 3, 2026: Applications open August 31, 2026: Application deadline September 21–25, 2026: Virtual masterclasses and startup clinics, beginning at 9:00am September 28–30, 2026: Physical event in Abuja featuring pitch competitions, exhibitions and investor deal rooms September 30, 2026: Regional finals and final pitches before the independent jury How to apply Eligible startup founders across ECOWAS Member States can apply through the official ECOWAS Startup Awards application portal. Applicants are advised to have all required documents ready before starting the process. The application form can be saved as applicants progress through it. The organisers have also published detailed guidelines containing the eligibility rules, application process, selection criteria and other requirements for participants. items.title: African unity is key to overcoming slavery’s enduring legacy – Dean Roberts Jnr
items.description: Amb. Prof. Dean Roberts Jnr has urged Africans at home and in the diaspora not to allow the legacy of slavery to continue dividing them, stressing that unity, reconciliation and a shared sense of identity are essential to the continent’s progress. Speaking at the Ibiaku Clan Development Association family retreat at the Villa Hilton Hotel in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria, he said Africans must resist the divisions created by the transatlantic slave trade and work together to strengthen their communities. The retreat was held on the theme: “Reclaiming Our Story – Ibiaku History, Identity and Heritage.” Amb. Prof. Roberts, who is the Continental Vice President of UNPGC-USA, described himself as a survivor of history rather than a victim, saying the effects of slavery continue to shape African societies and diaspora communities. He referred to the transatlantic slave trade as one of the gravest crimes committed against humanity and said its consequences went beyond the forced movement of millions of Africans. According to him, slavery broke families, erased identities and weakened communities, leaving deep social and historical scars. He said the strategy behind the slave trade was simple but destructive: divide people, weaken them and exploit them. Amb. Prof. Roberts therefore called on Africans to see themselves as one people and avoid internal divisions that could continue to undermine development. “Division destroys, but unity builds,” he said, warning that the effects of slavery could still be seen in poverty, land disputes, youth restiveness, cultism and other challenges confronting communities. He argued that these modern problems could become new forms of bondage if African communities failed to pursue unity, reconciliation and the breaking of generational cycles of conflict. Amb. Prof. Roberts also referred to Ghana’s push at the United Nations for international recognition of the trafficking and enslavement of Africans as a grave crime against humanity. He said the initiative underscored the need for African countries and people of African descent to confront the historical impact of slavery while building stronger relationships across borders. The retreat was also held in memory of the late Obong Elder Harry Etukudoh, whom Amb. Prof. Roberts described as a leader who chose to build his community despite the historical burdens inherited from slavery. He also cited the examples of prominent African and civil rights leaders, including Dr Kwame Nkrumah, Nelson Mandela, Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe, Chief Obafemi Awolowo, Sir Ahmadu Bello and Rev. Dr Martin Luther King Jr, as figures whose lives demonstrated the importance of unity, courage and collective purpose. In his closing remarks, Amb. Prof. Roberts pledged to use his international platforms to promote the identity and interests of Ibiaku. He said stronger cooperation among traditional leaders, residents, members of the diaspora and the younger generation would help the community move from exporting its human potential to developing it for the benefit of its people. He also expressed confidence that with committed leadership and collective support, Ibiaku could strengthen its identity, preserve its heritage and build a more united future.

items.title: Extended Producer Responsibility law to recognise and integrate informal waste collectors — EPA
items.description: The proposed Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) law is expected to recognise and integrate Ghana’s informal waste collectors into the country’s formal waste management system. Speaking at the JoyNews/IMANI Africa National Dialogue on Plastic Waste Management on August 11, Mr Larry Kotoe, Ag. Director for Sustainability and Circular Economy of the EPA, said the draft legislation has been designed to build on the existing contribution of informal waste operators, particularly their role in waste collection, rather than disrupt their activities. “We’ve actually designed the draft EPR law in such a way that it will have informal functions. We call it integration. They are already performing the role of collection. We don’t want to disrupt that, and they are very effective at that,” Mr Kotoe said. According to him, the focus would be on defining the appropriate role of informal operators within the EPR framework, particularly at the district assembly level, where local authorities and local government structures play an important role in waste management. Mr Kotoe stressed that traceability would be an important requirement under the proposed framework to ensure that collected waste can be tracked to its final destination. “If an informal sector cannot give us that traceability, then we need to assign them a different role where we can actually push the way that they collect to a place where we can trace it,” he explained. The approach is intended to ensure greater accountability within the waste management chain while allowing informal operators to continue contributing to waste collection. The draft EPR framework is also encouraging informal waste operators to organise themselves into cooperatives and associations. The official said such structures would make it easier for authorities and other stakeholders to identify, engage and work with informal operators collectively. “When they are performing their roles, we see them as a group and then incentivise them appropriately,” he said. The move is expected to create a more structured relationship between informal waste operators, local authorities and other stakeholders while improving coordination and accountability within the waste management sector. The proposed EPR law forms part of broader efforts to strengthen Ghana’s waste management system by ensuring that different actors within the value chain have clearly defined and coordinated roles.

items.title: NADMO says UAE $1m donation can support more than 91,000 flood victims
items.description: The National Disaster Management Organisation (NADMO) says its current relief stock is sufficient to support more than 91,000 people displaced by the June 29 floods. NADMO Director-General, Dr Joseph Bikanyi Kuyon, made the disclosure after the United Arab Emirates (UAE) presented relief items worth $1 million to the Government of Ghana on Monday, August 10. The donation, made through the UAE Office of the Minister of State for Climate Change and Sustainability in partnership with NADMO, is intended to support communities affected by the floods. The relief package includes 5,000 student mattresses, bags of rice and cooking oil. Receiving the items at the NADMO Head Office, Dr Kuyon said the UAE’s intervention had significantly strengthened the organisation’s capacity to respond to the needs of affected communities. “The United Arab Emirates came in as a government to support Ghana as a nation and that is why the relief support is so huge in that margin. I want to say that in that regard we have enough relief items to meet every victim’s need based on what we have received so far.” He said the latest supplies would enable NADMO to extend support to more than 91,000 displaced flood victims. Dr Kuyon, however, stressed the need for international partners to support Ghana not only after disasters but also in preparedness and prevention efforts. “NADMO needs you more when there is no disaster,” he said, arguing that early intervention was critical to reducing both the likelihood and severity of disasters. He said stronger support before disasters occur would help the country improve its preparedness and minimise the impact of future emergencies. Minister of State for Climate Change and Sustainability, Seidu Issifu, said the government was intensifying diplomatic efforts to secure additional assistance for flood-affected communities. He said Ghana had reached out to 67 embassies and was engaging up to 100 diplomatic missions as part of efforts to mobilise more resources. According to Mr Issifu, the government is also seeking technical assistance and equipment, rather than relying solely on food and other relief supplies. He said Japan was among the countries considering such support following discussions with its embassy. “Last week on Thursday I had a meeting with the Japanese embassy. They are looking at technical support. They are looking at support from giving equipment.” Mr Issifu said the equipment, when received, would be handed over to NADMO to strengthen its disaster response operations. “So what we are doing is not only distributing rice and sugar. We are expecting support in equipment so that we can present that to NADMO to assist them in the work that they are mandated to do,” he added. The UAE said the relief items were deliberately purchased from the Ghanaian market as part of efforts to support local businesses while providing assistance to flood victims. An official of the UAE Aid Agency, His Excellency Rashid Al Shamsi, Executive Director of Operations, said the decision was intended to contribute to Ghana’s economy. “To increase the economy of the country itself. This is the reason why we are buying from the market,” he said. Following the presentation, officials distributed some of the relief items directly to flood victims before touring the NADMO warehouse to inspect the available stock. The June 29 floods affected 38,802 people in the Greater Accra Region alone and displaced 7,761 households, according to figures presented to Parliament by the Ministry of the Interior. The latest intervention therefore comes as government and disaster management authorities continue efforts to provide relief to affected communities while strengthening preparedness against future flooding.

items.title: Réserves de blé : le dispositif réglementaire reste inachevé
items.description: Le Maroc dispose de plusieurs mois de réserves de blé tendre, mais le cadre qui encadre ces stocks reste incomplet. Dans son rapport annuel pour 2025, le CESE pointe notamment l’absence, depuis près de trois décennies, du texte réglementaire devant préciser leur composition, leur constitution et leur financement. Le Maroc dispose de stocks de sécurité de blé tendre capables de couvrir en moyenne trois à quatre mois de consommation. Mais derrière ce niveau de couverture, le CESE relève un dispositif encore marqué par des fragilités réglementaires et institutionnelles. Près de trois décennies après l’instauration du cadre juridique initial, les règles devant préciser les modalités de constitution, de financement et de gestion de ces réserves ne sont toujours pas complètement établies. Une dépendance aux importations qui renforce l’enjeu La question des stocks de sécurité prend une importance particulière dans un marché céréalier fortement exposé aux conditions extérieures. Selon le rapport annuel 2025 du Conseil économique, social et environnemental (CESE), le taux de dépendance du Maroc aux importations de céréales s’est établi en moyenne à près de 70% sur la période 2019-2023, contre 57% entre 2015 et 2019. Ce taux a même atteint 74% certaines années récentes. Cette dépendance rend l’approvisionnement national plus sensible aux fluctuations des marchés internationaux, aux perturbations des chaînes logistiques et aux aléas climatiques qui affectent la production nationale. Dans ce contexte, le niveau des stocks de sécurité de blé tendre constitue un élément central du dispositif. Le CESE indique qu’il se situe en moyenne entre trois et quatre mois de consommation. Ces volumes ont jusqu’à présent permis de répondre à la demande nationale, mais le Conseil appelle à un suivi plus régulier et à une vigilance renforcée, compte tenu de l’incertitude croissante des marchés internationaux et du niveau élevé de la consommation nationale. Un cadre réglementaire qui n’est toujours pas achevé Le marché des céréales est encadré par la loi n°12-94 du 22 février 1995 relative à l’Office national interprofessionnel des céréales et des légumineuses (ONICL) et à l’organisation du secteur. Ce dispositif confie à l’ONICL la mission de constituer un stock de sécurité en céréales ou d’en déléguer la constitution à des opérateurs privés. Ces derniers sont chargés, pour son compte, des opérations d’achat, de stockage et de vente. Le commerce des céréales étant libéralisé, les opérateurs restent toutefois tenus de déclarer à l’ONICL l’ensemble de leurs transactions. Dans les faits, relève le CESE, les stocks de sécurité demeurent majoritairement détenus par le secteur privé. C’est sur ce point que le rapport fait apparaître une faiblesse structurelle du dispositif. La législation avait prévu dès 1996, à travers le décret n°2-96-305, que les caractéristiques des stocks de sécurité soient fixées par voie réglementaire. Or, l’arrêté conjoint des ministres chargés des finances et de l’agriculture relatif à leur composition, leur constitution et leur financement n’a toujours pas été adopté. Le dispositif repose ainsi principalement sur des décisions ministérielles conjointes émises annuellement, en lien avec les activités de commercialisation et d’importation, ainsi que sur des circulaires annuelles de l’ONICL. Cette situation laisse donc subsister un cadre qui, selon le CESE, doit encore être parachevé pour donner une définition plus précise des règles applicables aux stocks de sécurité. Du système déclaratif à un contrôle renforcé Le Conseil relève également que le système repose largement sur un régime déclaratif : les opérateurs privés soumis à l’obligation de stockage déclarent leurs niveaux de stocks à l’ONICL. Cette organisation constitue l’un des points sur lesquels le CESE préconise une évolution. Parmi ses recommandations figure ainsi le renforcement des capacités de l’ONICL en matière de suivi, de gestion de l’approvisionnement et de renouvellement des stocks. Le Conseil propose également de substituer au système déclaratif un dispositif de contrôle renforcé, reposant sur des inspections régulières sur place, assorties de procès-verbaux et de sanctions dissuasives en cas d’infraction. Le CESE recommande parallèlement de préciser de manière exhaustive les règles applicables aux stocks de sécurité : leur composition, les mécanismes de constitution et de financement, les seuils par produit, ainsi que les obligations et responsabilités des différentes parties prenantes. Il propose également de renforcer les capacités de stockage à travers un modèle hybride associant des capacités publiques stratégiques portées par l’ONICL et des capacités privées, avec une répartition territoriale équilibrée des infrastructures. The post Réserves de blé : le dispositif réglementaire reste inachevé appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Private medical practitioners seek tax waivers on cancer treatment equipment
items.description: The Society of Private Medical and Dental Practitioners has called on the government to waive import duties and taxes on advanced cancer treatment equipment to help expand access to specialised care in Ghana. The Society says removing the financial burden associated with importing high-tech medical equipment would enable private healthcare providers to acquire modern technology and strengthen their capacity to diagnose and treat cancer. The call was made at the Society’s 45th Annual General Meeting in Ho, where health sector stakeholders discussed ways to improve healthcare delivery and strengthen collaboration between the public and private sectors. National President of the Society, Dr Andre Kwasi Kumah, said the government should not only waive the duties and taxes but also facilitate the speedy clearance of such equipment at the ports. “We, therefore, want to suggest to government to waive off import duties and taxes on such items and facilitate their ready discharge from the ports,” he said. Dr Kumah also called for additional financial support to enable private healthcare providers to invest in specialised equipment and expand service delivery. “We also wish for the government to provide a dedicated budgetary support for the private sector or provide financial guarantees that will enable the private sector to seek assistance from the banks,” he said. According to him, easier access to financing would help private health facilities make the investments required to support Ghana’s healthcare system. Call for stronger private-sector coordination Dr Kumah further proposed the establishment of an umbrella body for private-sector health groups under the Ministry of Health to improve coordination between private providers and government. He said a Chamber of Health should be established as soon as possible to provide a common platform for private healthcare organisations to engage more effectively with the Ministry of Health and other stakeholders. “In relation to this also, we also call on the government to facilitate the formation of an umbrella body of private sector groups under the Ministry of Health so that we can effectively coordinate such activities with the major stakeholder, which is the Ministry of Health, and in this light, we propose that the Chamber of Health be instituted as soon as possible,” he said. Government acknowledges private sector role Health Minister Kwamena Mintah Akandoh acknowledged the contribution of private healthcare providers to Ghana’s health sector, particularly in financing, service delivery, technology adoption, specialist care and job creation. “Private health providers continue to make significant contributions to health financing, service delivery, technology adoption, specialist care, and job creation. Your role in expanding access and improving the quality of care is widely recognised and appreciated,” he said. Mr Akandoh stressed the need for stronger collaboration between government and private healthcare providers in addressing the growing burden of cancer. “The Ministry of Health firmly believes that stronger collaboration between governments and the private sector is essential to effectively address the growing burden of cancer,” he said. UHAS Vice-Chancellor pushes research and early detection Vice-Chancellor of the University of Health and Allied Sciences, Prof Lydia Aziato, also underscored the importance of public education, early detection and research in improving cancer outcomes. She encouraged healthcare practitioners to incorporate research into their work and undertake studies that could help improve clinical practice. “I mentioned that it helps us to create awareness, health education, help us to detect any, and I’m adding the fact that you help us to refer any. I’m calling that you incorporate research, find some research, conduct some research to help in the area of practice as you have it,” she said. The discussions at the meeting highlighted the need for closer collaboration among government, private healthcare providers and academic institutions to strengthen Ghana’s response to cancer.

Evowheels, Yango hand over 15 Dongfeng Nammi 01 EVs to Ghanaian drivers under Drive-To-Own programme
items.description: Evowheels Ghana Motors and Yango Ride, part of the global technology company Yango Group, marked a significant milestone in Ghana’s green mobility journey with the handover of 15 DONGFENG NAMMI 01 electric vehicles to Yango partner drivers in Accra. The ceremony, themed “ Driving the Future Together in Ghana ,” adds to Yango’s electric vehicle fleet operations in the Ghanaian market and signals a new chapter for sustainable urban transport in the country. At the heart of the partnership is an innovative Drive-To-Own (DTO) model that sets it apart from conventional fleet programmes. Over a three-year period, Yango partner drivers operate their assigned DONGFENG NAMMI 01 electric vehicles and, at the end of the programme, own them outright, with no residual payment required. The model is designed to turn everyday driving into long-term asset ownership, directly improving financial security for drivers and their families. To support the transition to electric vehicles, Evowheels has introduced many exclusive benefits for the first batch of fleet drivers, including first-year comprehensive insurance, discounted fast charging at XChargeEV partner stations, a complimentary home charging solution, free chassis protection installation, monthly performance bonuses, VIP after-sales service at designated centres, official fleet uniforms, and in-car advertising revenue sharing from year two. The deployment marks another milestone as Yango strives to support sustainability in Ghana’s ride-hailing industry with clean, eco-friendly vehicles. For Evowheels, the partnership represents the successful introduction of high-quality Chinese new energy vehicles into the Ghanaian market, a first step toward a planned fleet of 100 electric vehicles within the next year. “This partnership is a strong step forward for green mobility in Ghana and for the drivers who power our platform,” the Head of Operations, Yango Rides in Africa, Timi Ayoade, said. “The Drive-To-Own model reflects our commitment to creating real economic opportunity for drivers, not just a job, but a path to owning an asset that can change their lives and support their families.” “‘Driving the Future Together’ is not just our slogan, it is our commitment to drivers, to the community, and to Ghana’s green future,” said William Huang, Country Manager of Evowheels Ghana Motors. “Through the DTO model and our comprehensive support policies, we aim to enable more drivers to embrace new energy vehicles, increase their income, and ultimately own their vehicles. We are confident in expanding our pure electric fleet to 100 units within the next year.” The Yango-Evowheels partnership demonstrates how a global technology platform, a local fleet operator, and structured vehicle financing can combine to accelerate electric vehicle adoption in a developing market. With professional EV after-sales support, a comprehensive driver benefits package, and a clear path to ownership, the programme is designed for long-term stability for drivers, for the platform, and for Ghana’s broader transition to cleaner urban transport. Yango continues to engage with fleet operators and entrepreneurs interested in building the next generation of electric mobility in Ghana.

items.title: Fouilles corporelles à nu : l’ASRED salue une mesure en faveur de la dignité des détenus
items.description: L’Association pour le soutien et la réinsertion sociale des détenus (ASRED) salue la décision des autorités judiciaires de mettre fin à la pratique systématique des fouilles corporelles à nu dans les établissements pénitentiaires. L’organisation y voit une avancée dans la modernisation du système carcéral et le respect des droits des personnes privées de liberté. Dans un communiqué publié ce 11 août 2026, l’association estime que cette mesure constitue « une avancée importante dans la modernisation de l’administration pénitentiaire et dans le respect de la dignité des personnes privées de liberté ». Pour l’organisation dirigée par Ibrahima Sall, la sécurité des établissements pénitentiaires reste une exigence essentielle, mais elle doit être conciliée avec le respect des droits humains, de l’intimité et de la dignité des détenus. Lire aussi: Prisons : fin de la fouille à nu des détenus à l’admission L’ASRED considère ainsi que le recours à des équipements technologiques adaptés pourrait permettre de renforcer les contrôles de sécurité tout en limitant les pratiques susceptibles d’être perçues comme humiliantes ou attentatoires à la dignité des personnes détenues. L’association rappelle également que cette orientation s’inscrit dans le prolongement des recommandations formulées au niveau international sur les conditions dans lesquelles doivent être effectuées les fouilles en milieu carcéral. Celles-ci doivent, selon elle, préserver autant que possible « la dignité et l’intimité des personnes détenues ». Des moyens et une formation pour accompagner la réforme L’ASRED félicite le ministère de la Justice et l’Administration pénitentiaire pour cette initiative et les encourage à poursuivre les efforts de modernisation des établissements pénitentiaires sénégalais. L’association appelle toutefois à accompagner cette réforme par un renforcement des moyens matériels et humains. Elle insiste également sur la nécessité d’assurer une formation continue des agents pénitentiaires afin de garantir une mise en œuvre « rigoureuse, professionnelle et respectueuse des droits fondamentaux ». Pour l’ASRED, la sécurité et la dignité des détenus ne doivent pas être opposées. « La sécurité et la dignité ne sont pas incompatibles : elles doivent avancer ensemble », affirme l’association. L’organisation réaffirme enfin sa disponibilité à accompagner les initiatives destinées à améliorer les conditions de détention, à protéger les droits des détenus et à moderniser le système pénitentiaire . A.N

items.title: Algérie : un géant chinois de l’acier pour relancer le complexe sidérurgique d’El Hadjar
items.description: L’Algérie fait de la relance du complexe sidérurgique d’El Hadjar à Annaba « une priorité stratégique ». La décision a été dévoilée jeudi 6 août par le ministre de l’Industrie, Yahia Bachir lors d’une visite de travail dans cette wilaya. Il a soutenu que la relance du géant algérien de l’acier est un « fondement essentiel pour le développement de l’industrie lourde ». Pour cela, l'Algérie va s'appuyer sur un géant mondial de l'acier. Quatre jours après cette visite, la Société nationale de sidérurgie (SNS), dont dépend ce complexe, a reçu lundi 10 août, une délégation du géant mondial de l’acier China Baowu Steel Group pour « discuter des perspectives de coopération stratégique dans le secteur sidérurgique ». China Baowu Steel Group pour relancer l’industrie sidérurgiques algérienne Slimane Arar, DG de la SNS a reçu lundi 10 août une délégation du plus grand producteur mondial d’acier avec des représentants de la China Road & Bridge Corporation (CRBC) Algérie. Au menu des discussions : un projet industriel intégré « d’importance stratégique, visant à développer un système sidérurgique intégral en Algérie, de la valorisation et l'exploitation du minerai de fer à sa transformation et sa production, en privilégiant le développement de produits à valeur ajoutée et la réduction de l’empreinte carbone », a expliqué la SNS. Lors de la réunion, les représentants de China Baowu Steel ont présenté la vision du groupe des différentes phases de développement de ce projet, ainsi que son « expertise et ses technologies en matière de réduction directe du minerai de fer, de production de fer préréduit (DRI) et de fer laminé à chaud (HBI), sans oublier ses solutions technologiques modernes et la digitalisation industrielle ». Les deux parties ont discuté également des « perspectives de développement d'une sidérurgie verte en Algérie, compte tenu des abondantes ressources minérales et énergétiques du pays, de son important potentiel en énergies renouvelables et de sa situation géographique stratégique, qui lui ouvre les portes des marchés régionaux et internationaux ». Les responsables de la SNS et du géant chinois de l’acier ont abordé les « mécanismes de coopération en matière de transfert de technologies et d’expertise, de formation et de développement des compétences, ainsi que de localisation de l’activité industrielle ». Ils ont aussi discuté du renforcement de « l’intégration locale » et de l’implication des « capacités et institutions nationales aux différentes étapes de la mise en œuvre et du développement des projets futurs ». Si aucun contrat n’a été signé, la SNS et China Baowu Steel sont convenus de « poursuivre les consultations, les études techniques relatives au projet et d’approfondir les différents aspects industriels, technologiques et économiques afin d’identifier les meilleures façons de concrétiser les opportunités de coopération et de partenariat ». Vers un partenariat SNS – China Baowu Steel Group : les prochaines étapes Pour la SNS, cette visite de la délégation du géant mondial de l’acier constitue une « étape importante » dans les consultations entre les deux parties. « Les prochaines phases devraient aboutir à l'élaboration d'une feuille de route commune pour des études complémentaires et à l'identification des domaines de coopération prioritaires, ouvrant la voie à la réflexion sur leur mise en œuvre dans le cadre de futurs partenariats industriels », a-t-elle précisé, en soulignant que l’industrie algérienne vise à se « positionner au sein des chaînes de valeur mondiales de la sidérurgie verte ». Complexe d’El Hadjar : une base industrielle, mais des installations obsolètes Le complexe sidérurgique d’El Hadjar a été lancé en 1969 dans le cadre des grands projets pour industrialiser le pays. En 2001, il a été cédé au groupe indien Ispat, devenu MittalSteel. Une expérience marquée par un échec, puisque le géant indien a quitté l’Algérie sans moderniser le complexe d’El Hadjar qui a été récupéré par l’État. Cet énorme complexe » possède une base industrielle considérable et des potentialités importantes bien que certaines de ses installations sont arrivées au terme de leur longévité supposée' ', a dit le ministre de l’Industrie, selon l’agence APS . Cette situation nécessite le lancement d’un » programme urgent de modernisation et de remplacement de certains équipements pour répondre aux critères mondiaux en termes de productivité, d’efficience et de compétitivité ». items.title: ¿Dónde habrá nubes durante el eclipse? Consulte cómo estarán los cielos y el horizonte en cada municipio
items.description: Las nubes bajas pueden convertirse en el peor enemigo de alguien que quiera ver el eclipse de este 12 de agosto. En el siguiente mapa mostramos dos modelos que estiman la nubosidad prevista para las 20 horas del miércoles en cada municipio y hacia el horizonte, además del detalle de altura de las nubes. La última previsión disponible se actualizó la mañana de este martes e incorpora los datos horarios de AEMET, de alta resolución. Seguir leyendo Metodología del mapa El mapa muestra una previsión de nubosidad para la hora del eclipse en cada punto de España. La capa visible representa la nubosidad total prevista por el modelo del Centro Europeo de Predicción a Medio Plazo (ECMWF), distribuido por AEMET a través de CEPPM. Su resolución aproximada es de 5 kilómetros. Dese el martes, el mapa incorporará también HARMONIE-AROME, el modelo de alta resolución de AEMET. Su rejilla, de aproximadamente 2,5 kilómetros, permite consultar la nubosidad prevista por horas concretas con más detalle local que el modelo europeo de medio plazo. Las fichas de cada lugar combinan dos tipos de información. Por un lado la nubosidad total prevista en ese punto por CEPPM, expresada en intervalos de porcentaje; y por otro la estructura vertical media de las nubes en el municipio según AIFS , el modelo de inteligencia artificial del ECMWF, con una resolución aproximada de 25 kilómetros (distingue entre nubes bajas, medias y altas) La clasificación de las condiciones —favorable, regular o desfavorable— combina la nubosidad total del punto con la proporción de nubes bajas, medias y altas prevista sobre el municipio. El cálculo da más peso a las nubes bajas, un peso intermedio a las medias y menor a las altas. La ficha municipal no suma las tres capas de AIFS: las nubes bajas, medias y altas pueden coexistir a distintas alturas. Se muestran como una descripción de la estructura vertical prevista, no como partes excluyentes de un mismo 100%. El modo “Vista al horizonte” es una estimación complementaria. Calcula la dirección y altura del Sol en el máximo local del eclipse y toma tres muestras de nube baja AIFS en la línea de visión, a alturas aproximadas de entre 1 y 2 kilómetros. Muestra el escenario más nuboso de esas muestras. Es una orientación sobre posibles nubes entre el observador y el Sol, no una predicción detallada del relieve ni de la visibilidad exacta.

items.title: Ghana spends 0.084% of expenditure on creative industry – JoyNews Research
items.description: Ghana spends just 0.084% of its overall expenditure on the creative industry, according to JoyNews Research. Head of Research at JoyNews , Isaac Kofi Agyei, highlighted the level of government spending tourism, culture and creative arts during his presentation at the ninth edition of Joy FM’s Showbiz Roundtable . “It is sad that we are spending just about 0.084% of the national cake on the creative industry. That is how much we are spending on a sector that is expected to bring in some 5 billion dollars in every year. In fact, if you are ranking the top foreign exchange earners for this country, you can put it at number two or number three,” he said. He explained that the government is spending GH¢255 million on the sector, which represents 0.084% of overall expenditure. Kofi’s presentation laid the foundation for the roundtable discussion themed “Assessing 20 Months of Government’s Impact on Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts.” The programme examined the government’s commitments to the sector, assessed the level of implementation, measured the impact of policies and explored the road ahead for Ghana’s creative economy. The discussion featured industry figures including Chief Operating Officer of Maestro Africa Group, Francis Doku; Lead Consultant at Jesse Agyepong and Associates, Jesse Agyepong; pop culture journalist Olele Salvador; and Joy FM broadcaster Ken Addy. Also in attendance were comedians Lekzy DeComic, Kojo Pjay, Percy Obrempong, James Brown and Jacinta. Others were broadcasters Austine Woode and Kojo Preko Dankwah, while tourism professional Emmanuel Frimpong was also present. The discussion was moderated by broadcaster and arts and culture journalist Kwame Dadzie. It was produced by Philip Nai, with support from Anita Teye and Idah Lamaire.

items.title: The Pakistan the world keeps missing
items.description: International standards are often assumed to be a modern invention. They are not. Many predate the United Nations itself; the International Labour Organization (ILO), for instance, was established under the League of Nations and only later folded into the UN system. Countries have long used such standards to strengthen governance, build credibility, and integrate into the global economy. Pakistan has been one of them. Over the decades, it has voluntarily become a party to numerous international treaties and conventions, incorporating many of their provisions into its Constitution, national legislation, and regulatory framework, including constitutional guarantees relating to fundamental rights, labour protections and environmental governance. It is, however, worth remembering that joining an international treaty is a sovereign, voluntary decision. Pakistan took on these obligations because they were seen as consistent with its long-term development goals, not because it was compelled to. Today, the country is party to well over 150 major international treaties, conventions, and protocols spanning governance, trade, labour, human rights, environmental protection, maritime affairs, and more. Far from being symbolic, these commitments strengthen market access, attract international investment, support development cooperation and trade negotiations, and reassure global buyers about the credibility of Pakistan’s regulatory framework. Many of them, notably, were undertaken decades before concepts like ESG, carbon border measures, and supply-chain due diligence became central to global trade. The labour record: ahead of the pack Pakistan’s commitment to international labour standards illustrates this long-standing pattern well. The country has ratified 38 ILO conventions and one protocol, including eight of the 10 Fundamental Conventions — covering the abolition of forced labour, minimum working age, freedom of association, collective bargaining, equal remuneration, non-discrimination, and the elimination of child labour. The remaining two — Convention No. 155 on Occupational Safety and Health and Convention No. 187 on the Promotional Framework for Occupational Safety and Health — are currently under active consideration for ratification. Pakistan has also ratified two of the four ILO Governance (Priority) Conventions, on labour inspection and tripartite consultation. Why does this matter? Because labour standards increasingly determine market access, particularly for export-oriented economies in Asia. Pakistan has also ratified the Protocol of 2014 to the Forced Labour Convention, signalling its commitment to global best practices and reassuring international buyers that its exports meet internationally recognised labour standards. Tellingly, India has not yet ratified this protocol, despite its labour-related commitments under its free trade agreement with the European Union. Several major Asian textile and apparel exporters — including China, Vietnam, and Cambodia — have not ratified it either, despite being far more deeply integrated into global value chains than Pakistan. Beyond labour: environment and the wider picture Labour is only one part of Pakistan’s broader compliance landscape. The country is also party to 15 major Multilateral Environmental Agreements (MEAs), covering climate change, biodiversity conservation, hazardous chemicals and waste management, ozone layer protection, desertification, and cultural and natural heritage. The scale of this engagement becomes clearer when viewed over time. The chart below traces the cumulative growth of Pakistan’s international commitments since independence and it shows a country that has, year after year, steadily expanded its participation in international legal frameworks. Committing to international standards is no simple undertaking. Ratifying a treaty is only the beginning; it requires governments to review their domestic legal framework and, where necessary, amend legislation, strengthen institutions, and align national policies with international obligations. Pakistan’s 18th Constitutional Amendment, for example, devolved many environmental and labour-related responsibilities to the provinces, creating an extensive compliance architecture that runs from federal ministries down to provincial departments and, ultimately, local governments. The challenges are real None of this has been easy, and challenges remain. Even the world’s most advanced economies have yet to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals; Pakistan is no exception. Part of the reason is that many international standards are negotiated and implemented within sophisticated legal and regulatory systems that are more readily supported by advanced economies. Less developed economies, by contrast, often face additional implementation hurdles owing to resource constraints and competing development priorities. These challenges are compounded by Pakistan’s geopolitical environment. Sharing borders with India and Afghanistan, the country continues to contend with persistent security concerns and regional instability, adding further pressure on its institutions. Despite these constraints, Pakistan has repeatedly shown a willingness to update its compliance frameworks in line with emerging global expectations. International law keeps evolving in response to new global challenges, geopolitical developments, increasingly stringent trade rules, and more complex global value chains. Most recently, in response to concerns raised by the United States over the risk of forced labour in global supply chains, Pakistan promptly amended its Import Policy Order to prohibit the import of goods produced wholly or partly using forced labour, well before India or Bangladesh adopted comparable measures. As a result, imported products containing inputs produced through forced labour at any stage of the value chain are now barred from entering Pakistan’s market. The story behind the numbers The graph above tells only part of the story. Behind every point on it lie years of negotiations, legal reforms, institutional strengthening, and policy decisions. Their impact is rarely visible overnight, but none of that work has gone to waste. Perhaps it is time to recognise that Pakistan’s engagement with international standards is not a recent phenomenon. It has been quietly laying the foundations for sustainable development for decades. And this is the Pakistan we must not overlook.

items.title: Hearts of Oak pull out of GHALCA Top-4 as Samartex take their place
items.description: Hearts of Oak will not participate in this year’s GHALCA Top-4 Tournament after the club decided that the competition’s schedule does not fit with its preparations for the new Ghana Premier League season. The Phobians announced their withdrawal on Tuesday, 11 August 2026, just over two weeks before the tournament is due to begin. “After careful consideration, the Club has therefore decided that withdrawing from the tournament is the most appropriate course of action at this time,” the statement said. GHALCA has subsequently named FC Samartex 1996 as Hearts’ replacement. Samartex finished fifth in the Ghana Premier League last season and will now take the place of the Accra giants in the four-team pre-season competition. “We have decided to replace Hearts of Oak with FC Samartex, who finished fifth on the league log last season,” GHALCA chairman John Ansah told Asempa FM. items.title: NFF apologises to President Tinubu, Nigerians over WAFCON setback
items.description: By Emmanuel Okogba The Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) has issued a formal apology to the Federal Government and the people of Nigeria following the Super Falcons’ failure to secure direct qualification for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup at the ongoing Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON). In a statement on behalf of the NFF Executive Committee, the Super Falcons and the entire Nigerian football family, NFF President Alhaji Ibrahim Musa Gusau expressed deep regret over the result. “We recognise the disappointment this result has caused millions of Nigerians who passionately support and identify with the Super Falcons,” Gusau said. “The team went into the competition carrying the hopes of the nation and the enormous goodwill and support of the Federal Government, and we regret that we were unable to deliver the result expected at this stage.” The NFF extended a special apology to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, noting his strong support for Nigerian sports and women athletes in particular. “Mr. President has demonstrated an exceptional commitment to Nigerian sports and, particularly, to the development and welfare of women in sports,” the statement said. It recalled the substantial rewards, national honours, houses and reception given to the Super Falcons after their previous WAFCON triumph, as well as continued support for the Super Eagles. “It is therefore with genuine humility and regret that we acknowledge that we have not been able to repay that confidence with the outcome expected at this stage of the competition. We sincerely apologise to Mr. President and deeply appreciate his continued interest, encouragement and investment in Nigerian football.” The federation also apologised to the National Assembly, the National Sports Commission, sponsors, stakeholders and Nigerian supporters at home and abroad. Despite the setback, the NFF said a pathway remains open through the CAF play-offs for two tickets, followed by the FIFA play-off tournament. “We must now regroup, learn from this setback and focus completely on the opportunity that remains,” Gusau said. “The NFF, technical team and players are committed to doing everything within their power to secure Nigeria’s place at the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup.” The federation pledged an honest assessment of preparation, technical planning, logistics and overall operations to identify areas for improvement. “We hear the disappointment of Nigerians, we share it and we accept our responsibility. But we are not giving up,” the statement added. “Our resolve is to ensure that the Super Falcons return stronger, fight harder and do everything possible to make Mr. President, the Federal Government and Nigerians proud once again.” The NFF thanked Nigerians for their support and urged continued backing for the Super Falcons as they pursue the remaining route to the 2027 World Cup. The post NFF apologises to President Tinubu, Nigerians over WAFCON setback appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: UEFA Super Cup: PSG, Aston Villa set to clash as Somali referee Artan makes history
items.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Paris Saint-Germain and Aston Villa will battle for the UEFA Super Cup in Salzburg, Austria, on Wednesday, with Somali referee Omar Artan set to become the first non-European official to take charge of the prestigious fixture. The annual encounter pits the reigning Champions League winners against the Europa League champions, with PSG seeking to become only the second team in the modern era to successfully defend the title after Real Madrid achieved the feat in 2016 and 2017. PSG defeated Tottenham Hotspur on penalties in last year’s final. However, Artan’s appointment has added another layer of interest to Wednesday’s game after the 34-year-old was prevented from officiating at the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the United States. Artan was among the officials selected for the tournament but was barred from entering the US days before the competition began. US officials cited vetting and national security concerns, including alleged links to terrorist organisations, although no evidence was publicly provided. UEFA subsequently selected Artan to referee the Super Cup, a decision that has been widely welcomed within the football community. The appointment comes after Artan was recognised as Africa’s leading referee last season. He also officiated the 2025 African Champions League final. Reflecting on the difficult period surrounding his World Cup exclusion, Artan said the experience had been challenging but expressed gratitude for the support he received. “A lot of people have sympathy for me because when someone has been working a lot of years and is supposed to do something, and then can’t do it, it’s very challenging,” he told UEFA. “I really appreciate the support I received throughout the world, though. I’m so grateful.” Artan said he had been studying both teams extensively ahead of his first assignment in European football. “The standard in Europe is fantastic and the football they play is very, very good,” he said. PSG’s preparations have been influenced by the late return of several of their players who featured prominently at the 2026 World Cup. Ballon d’Or winner Ousmane Dembélé returned to training on Monday alongside France teammates Désiré Doué and Bradley Barcola. Spain midfielder Fabián Ruiz has also resumed training after helping his country win the World Cup. Georgian winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, whose country did not qualify for the tournament, has been back in training for longer and is expected to start. New signing Maghnes Akliouche could also feature, although Barcola has been linked with a move to Liverpool. PSG may additionally hand a debut to former Aston Villa defender Lucas Digne, who joined the French club on Sunday for a reported €10m ($11.6m). Aston Villa, meanwhile, will begin the new campaign with several changes to their squad under manager Unai Emery. The club lost midfielders Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans to Chelsea and Manchester United respectively, while Digne also departed for PSG. Villa have brought in Swiss World Cup player Johan Manzambi and Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes from relegated Wolverhampton Wanderers. Manzambi, however, is unavailable because of a knee injury. Villa booked their place in the Super Cup after defeating Freiburg 3-0 in the Europa League final. The match will also mark their second Champions League campaign under Emery, who previously coached PSG. With PSG aiming to add another European trophy and Villa looking to make their mark on the continental stage, Wednesday’s encounter promises a compelling start to the new European season — with Artan at the centre of a historic refereeing moment. items.title: Violence des gangs en Haïti: les organisations de femmes fragilisées par les coupes dans l’aide
items.description: Les violences des gangs en Haïti qui s'étendent désormais bien au-delà de la capitale Port-au-Prince plongent les femmes haïtiennes dans une spirale où se mêlent déplacements forcés, violences sexuelles et extrême précarité. Alors que près de 1,47 million de personnes ont dû fuir leur foyer, dont 790.000 femmes et filles, les organisations dirigées par des femmes constituent souvent le dernier rempart pour les survivantes. Mais leur action est aujourd'hui fragilisée par les coupes dans l'aide internationale. À Ouanaminthe, dans le nord-est du pays, Roselène Pierre en fait l'expérience chaque jour. Présidente du Rassemblement des femmes engagées de Ouanaminthe (RFEO), soutenu par ONU Femmes , elle est disponible jour et nuit pour venir en aide aux femmes et aux enfants victimes des violences. «Les femmes sont battues, il y a des violences sexuelles contre les femmes, et les femmes meurent», résume-t-elle dans des propos recueillis par ONU Femmes. Fondée il y a près de vingt ans, son organisation accueille aujourd'hui un nombre croissant de survivantes, déplacées par les affrontements ou renvoyées de République dominicaine. «C'est une prise en charge complète », explique Mme Pierre. « Nous les accueillons, nous les enregistrons, nous leur offrons un hébergement temporaire, des kits d'hygiène, des vêtements, des sous-vêtements, un moyen de transport… Puis nous leur apportons un soutien psychologique.» Le choix impossible de la survie Au-delà de l'urgence, les femmes déplacées doivent aussi faire face à une précarité extrême. Emmanuela a fui Mirebalais avec son grand-père et des centaines de voisins. Après avoir passé plusieurs semaines cachée dans la forêt, elle a trouvé refuge dans un site de déplacés à Fort-Liberté. Elle décrit à ONU Femmes les choix déchirants auxquels certaines femmes sont confrontées: «Certaines ont des enfants, et quand les enfants pleurent, elles sont obligées de vendre leur corps pour s'occuper d'eux.» Selon les dernières données de l'agence onusienne, plus de 80 % des femmes vivant dans les sites de déplacement en Haïti sont sans emploi. Les gangs exploitent cette pauvreté et utilisent menaces et intimidations pour contraindre des femmes et des filles à rejoindre leurs rangs ou à les servir. © ONU Femmes/Jess DiPierro Obert Fania Finfin, présidente du Groupe féministe révolté d'Haïti (GFRD), dirige un groupe de soutien aux femmes avec une collègue à Ouanaminthe, dans le nord-est d'Haïti. La peur de devenir la «femme» d'un chef de gang Katiana a quitté Port-au-Prince après que des membres d'un gang ont pris le contrôle de son quartier et tué sous ses yeux un voisin et ami. Réfugiée à Ouanaminthe, elle a bénéficié du soutien du RFEO, notamment d'un accompagnement psychologique, d'une formation et d'une aide financière. Mais ce qui la hante reste ce qui aurait pu lui arriver si elle était restée. «Certaines femmes sont violées et forcées de devenir les épouses de certains chefs de gangs… Si j'étais restée là-bas, je n'ose pas imaginer ce qui aurait pu m'arriver.» Retrouver la vie À 43 ans, Loudmia a elle aussi fui Port-au-Prince lorsque les gangs ont envahi son quartier, incendié sa maison et détruit tout ce qu'elle possédait. «J'ai perdu mon frère. J'ai perdu mon cousin. J'ai perdu ma tante. Et j'ai perdu mes amis, beaucoup de personnes. Ils leur ont tiré dessus, ils les ont brûlés. Ils ont incendié leurs maisons», raconte-t-elle. Livrée à elle-même avec ses trois enfants, elle vivait dans la rue lorsqu'une amie l'a conduite au RFEO. «C'est grâce à cette amie qui m'a amenée au RFEO qu'aujourd'hui je suis ici. Je suis en vie.» Au sein de l'organisation, Loudmia participe à des séances de soutien psychologique et a reçu une petite subvention en espèces pour recommencer sa vie. «Ils me parlent de ce qu'est la vie. Ils m'aident à retrouver mes souvenirs, pour que je ne garde pas ce choc dans ma tête tout le temps, en moi-même, pour que je n'y pense pas tout le temps.» Elle ne cache pas son admiration pour Roselène Pierre: «Après Dieu, je considérerais Madame Roselène du RFEO comme une reine.» © ONU Femmes/Jess DiPierro Obert Philonia marche avec des employés d'ONU Femmes à Cap-Haïtien, en Haïti. Des besoins en hausse, des moyens en baisse Alors que les besoins explosent, les organisations de femmes voient leurs ressources fondre. Le RFEO fait partie des nombreuses associations contraintes de réduire leurs effectifs, limitant ainsi le nombre de femmes et d'enfants qu'elles peuvent accompagner. Une enquête menée par ONU Femmes montre que 83 % des organisations de femmes ont perdu du personnel, tandis qu'environ deux tiers ont dû retarder ou suspendre leurs services aux survivantes de violences fondées sur le genre. Plus de 95% estiment que leurs capacités sont désormais inférieures aux besoins, et une organisation sur trois craint de devoir suspendre ses activités ou fermer dans les douze prochains mois. Malgré ces difficultés, ONU Femmes poursuit son appui aux organisations dirigées par des femmes à travers le pays. En collaboration avec ses partenaires, l'agence soutient des services de prise en charge psychosociale, des transferts monétaires permettant aux femmes de créer de petites activités génératrices de revenus, l'accès à une aide essentielle, ainsi que des initiatives de protection, de prévention et de relèvement au sein des communautés. Source: ONU Info L’article Violence des gangs en Haïti: les organisations de femmes fragilisées par les coupes dans l'aide est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .
